LABEL: abated steam reforming hydrogen
definition: Abated steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is output of a steam reforming process which is followed by a carbon capture and storage process.

LABEL: abbreviation
definition: An abbreviation is a symbol of a textual entity.

LABEL: AC-line
definition: An AC-line is a powerline for transferring high voltage alternating current.

LABEL: acceptance
definition: Acceptance is a realizable entity that represents the attitude of a person or organisation with respect to a certain constructional, (infra)structural or political measure that may be realized in, affected by or results of complex processes like discussions, communications, transformative measures or former personal experiences.

LABEL: account for wake losses
definition: Account for wake losses is an action specification that describes the inclusion of losses due to wind turbine wake effects, which reduce wind speed and energy yield behind turbines.

LABEL: acronym
definition: An acronym is an abbreviation of the title by using the first letters of each part of the title.

LABEL: action specification
definition: A directive information entity that describes an action the bearer will take.

LABEL: action specification for techno-economic potential
definition: Action specification for techno-economic potential is an action specification that deals with techno-economic potential.

LABEL: action specification for the feasible potential
definition: Action specification for the feasible potential is an action specification that deals with the feasible potential of something.

LABEL: action specification for the technical wind potential
definition: Action specification for the technical wind potential of the available area is an action specification that deals with the technical wind potential of the available area.

LABEL: action specification for wind characteristics
definition:
Action specification for wind characteristics is an action specification that deals with wind characteristics.
Wind characteristics include speed, direction, frequency, turbulence, and seasonal or diurnal patterns.

LABEL: action specification for wind farm development area
definition: Action specification for wind farm development area is an action specification that deals with available area for wind farm development.

LABEL: adsorption
definition: Adsorption is a process that leads to an accumulation of a substance within a phase or at an interface between two phases.

LABEL: aerothermal energy
definition: Aerothermal energy is a natural ambient thermal energy that is stored in the air of a natural environment.

LABEL: agent
definition: Agent is a role of a person or organisation that directs its activity towards achieving goals.

LABEL: aggregation type
definition: An aggregation type is a data descriptor that contains information on the aggregation method applied on a data set.

LABEL: agriculture, forestry and land use sector
definition: A agriculture, forestry and land use (AFOLU) sector is a sector that covers activities and natural processes from agriculture, forestry, land use and land use change.

LABEL: air
definition: Air is a gas mixture that forms the Earth's atmosphere.

LABEL: air density adjustment
definition: Air density adjustment is an action specification that describes how variations in air density due to changes in altitude, temperature, and pressure are incorporated into the wind resource calculations.

LABEL: air pollutant
definition: An air pollutant is a portion of matter that participates in some air pollution.

LABEL: air pollution
definition: Air pollution occurs when harmful or excessive quantities of substances including gases, particles, and biological molecules are introduced into Earth's atmosphere.

LABEL: aircraft
definition: An aircraft is a vehicle that is flying in the air.

LABEL: airplane
definition: An airplane is an aircraft that has fixed wings.

LABEL: airport
definition: An airport is a transport hub for airplanes.

LABEL: algorithm
definition: A plan specification which describes the inputs and output of mathematical functions as well as workflow of execution for achieving an predefined objective. Algorithms are realized usually by means of implementation as computer programs for execution by automata.

LABEL: ambient thermal energy
definition: Ambient thermal energy is thermal energy that is stored in the ambient air, beneath the surface of solid earth or in surface water. It is captured by heat pumps.

LABEL: ambient thermal energy transfer
definition: Ambient thermal energy transfer is a heat transfer from the ambient air to a transportable material entity.

LABEL: ambiguous uncertainty
definition: Ambiguous uncertainty is a nature of model uncertainty that stems from multiple frames of reference about a phenomenon existing similtaneously.

LABEL: ammonia
definition: Ammonia is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NH3. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

LABEL: amortisation time
definition: An amortisation time is the time span in which the investment costs are refinanced from the annual profits and depreciation of the investment.

LABEL: amount
definition: An amount is a quality of an object aggregate that counts the number of entities that form the object aggregate.

LABEL: ampere
definition: "An electric current unit which is equal to the constant current which, if maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length, of negligible circular cross-section, and placed 1 m apart in vacuum, would produce between these conductors a force equal to 2 x 10^[-7] newton per meter of length." [BIPM:BIPM, NIST:NIST]

LABEL: analysis scope
definition: An analysis scope is an information content entity that describes the boundaries of what a study or scenario covers.

LABEL: analytical approach
definition: A analytical approach is a model descriptor that contains information about the analysis strategy of a model.

LABEL: angle unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the figure or space formed by the junction of two lines or planes." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: annual
definition: one value per year

LABEL: Annual Emission Allocation
definition: An Annual Emission Allocation (AEA) is an emission certificate used in the Effort Sharing Decision (ESD) and the Effort Sharing Regulation (ESR). It permits the emission of a CO2 equivalent quantity of 1 tonne.

LABEL: annual GDP growth
definition: Annual GDP growth is an economic value that quantifies the difference between GDP in one year compared to the previous year.

LABEL: anthracite
definition: Anthracite is a hard coal with a high caloric value due to its high carbon content (about 90 % fixed carbon).

LABEL: anthropogenic
definition: Anthropogenic is an origin of portions of matter or energies created by human activity.

LABEL: apinist
definition: An apinist is an OEP user who mainly interacts via an API.

LABEL: application programming interface
definition: An application programming interface (API) is a software interface allowing two software applications to communicate with each other.

LABEL: apply socio-economic constraints for assessment of potential
definition: Apply socio-economic constraints for assessment of potential is an action specification that describes the process of integrating non-technical factors, such as social acceptance, land use regulations, or market conditions, into the potential assessment.

LABEL: arable land
definition: An arable land is a region of relevance which is regularly manipulated by human activities, such as plowing or tilling, in order to grow crops.

LABEL: arable land with high soil quality
definition: An arable land with high soil quality is an arable land having some soil as part that can be categorized as having high soil quality.

LABEL: arable land with poor soil quality
definition: An arable land with poor soil quality is an arable land having some soil as part that can be categorized as having poor soil quality.

LABEL: area density unit
definition: "A density unit which is a standard measure of the mass exerting an influence on a given area." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: area per power unit
definition: An area per power unit is a unit which is a measure for an area per nameplate capacity.

LABEL: area unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the amount of a 2-dimensional flat surface." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: area value
definition: An area value is a quantity value indicating the size of a two-dimensional spatial region.

LABEL: areal energy density
definition: An areal energy density is a quantity value that states a certain energy amount per area.

LABEL: areal energy density unit
definition: An areal energy density unit is a unit which is a measure for the energy per surface area.

LABEL: areal power density
definition: An areal power density is a quantity value that indicates a certain power per area.

LABEL: areal power density unit
definition: An areal power density unit is a unit which is a measure for the power per surface area.

LABEL: areal solar energy density
definition: An areal solar energy density is an areal energy density that gives the arriving solar energy per area. A synonym for areal solar energy density is irradiation.

LABEL: areal solar power density
definition: An areal solar power density is an areal power density that indicates the arriving solar power per area. A synonym for areal solar power density is irradiance.

LABEL: arithmetic mean
definition: average value calculated by arithmetic mean over a set of data values, e.g. within a time step or spatial region

LABEL: artificial ambient thermal energy
definition: Artificial ambient thermal energy is ambient thermal energy that has an anthropogenic origin.

LABEL: artificial object
definition: An artificial object is an object that was deliberately manufactured by humans to address a particular purpose.

LABEL: associated gas
definition: Associated gas is a natural gas that is a byproduct from crude oil exploitation.

LABEL: assumption
definition: An assumption is an information content entity about a property of a system or process. It determines a part of a scenario content.

LABEL: atto
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of 10 to the power of -18." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: author
definition: An author is an agent that creates or has created written work.

LABEL: aviation gasoline
definition: Aviation gasoline is gasoline used as motor spirit and prepared especially for aviation piston engines, with an octane number suited to the engine, a freezing point of -60 °C and a distillation range usually within the limits of 30 °C and 180 °C.

LABEL: aviation network
definition: An aviation network is a transport network that enables air transport.

LABEL: award
definition: An award is a document that signifies that a supplier for a particular commodity or service specified in a bid has been accepted.

LABEL: B7
definition: B7 is a diesel fuel that consists of fossil diesel fuel and up to 7 % biodiesel and that is liquid.

LABEL: base unit
definition: "A unit which is one of a particular measure to which all measures of that type can be related." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: battery
definition: A battery is an energy storage object using different chemical or physical reactions to store energy.

LABEL: battery electric car
definition: A battery electric car is a car that has an electric traction motor and a traction battery and thus is also a battery electric vehicle.

LABEL: battery electric truck
definition: A battery electric truck is a truck that has an electric traction motor and a traction battery and thus is also a battery electric vehicle.

LABEL: battery electric vehicle
definition: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) is an electric vehicle that stores energy in a traction battery.

LABEL: bicycle
definition: A bicycle is a road vehicle that has two wheels and is propelled by a person.

LABEL: bid
definition: A bid is a document describing an offer made by an agent to another agent in an effort to exchange commodities or services via terms relating to price and quantity which will be part of the resulting contract.

LABEL: bidding zone
definition: A bidding zone is a two-dimensional spatial region in which market participants are able to exchange energy without capacity allocation.

LABEL: bidding zone role
definition: A bidding zone role is a role of a two-dimensional spatial region that is realised in market participants trading energy without capacity allocation.

LABEL: bidirectional vehicle charging station
definition: A bidirectional vehicle charging station is a vehicle charging station that can also feed electrical energy from the traction battery back into the electricity grid.

LABEL: binary file format
definition: A binary file format is a file format that is not a text format.

LABEL: biodiesel
definition: Biodiesel is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a diesel fuel role. It is produced from plants or animals and thus has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: bioenergy
definition: Bioenergy is chemical energy that is stored in biofuels.

LABEL: bioethanol
definition: Bioethanol is ethanol with a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biofuel
definition: A biofuel is a combustion fuel that has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biofuel power plant
definition: A biofuel power plant is a power plant that has biofuel power units as parts.

LABEL: biofuel power unit
definition: A biofuel power unit is a power generating unit using biofuel.

LABEL: biogas
definition: Biogas is a gas mixture produced by anaerobic digestion. It consists mainly of methane and carbon dioxide and can be used as fuel.

LABEL: biogas power plant
definition: A biogas power plant is a biofuel power plant that has biogas power units as parts.

LABEL: biogas power unit
definition: A biogas power unit is a biofuel power unit using biogas as fuel.

LABEL: biogasoline
definition: Biogasoline is a portion of matter that has a liquid state of matter and has a gasoline fuel role. It consists of bioethanol, biomethanol and products of these two substances. It is made from vegetable or animal material and thus has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biogenic
definition: Biogenic is an origin of portions of matter made by or produced from life forms.

LABEL: biogenic industrial waste fuel
definition: A biogenic industrial waste fuel is an industrial waste fuel that has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biogenic municipal waste fuel
definition: A biogenic municipal waste fuel is a municipal waste fuel that has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biogenic waste fuel
definition: A biogenic waste fuel is a waste fuel that has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biomass
definition: Biomass is a portion of matter from plants or animals and has thus has a biogenic origin.

LABEL: biomethane
definition: Biomethane is a gas mixture produced from biogas by removing carbon dioxide. It consists mainly of methane and can be used as fuel.

LABEL: biosphere reserve
definition: A biosphere reserve is a protected area that has the biosphere reserve role, i.e. it is protected for conserving biodiversity, promoting sustainable development, and supporting research and education, within the UNESCO "Man and the Biosphere" (MAB) Programme.

LABEL: biosphere reserve role
definition: A biosphere reserve role is a protected area role for areas, aimed at conserving biodiversity, promoting sustainable development, and supporting research and education, within the UNESCO "Man and the Biosphere" (MAB) Programme.

LABEL: bird sanctuary
definition: A bird sanctuary is a protected area that has the bird sanctuary role, which is aimed at protecting and conserving endangered and migratory bird species, within the European "Natura 2000" network of protected areas.

LABEL: bird sanctuary role
definition: A bird sanctuary role is a protected area role for areas, aimed at protecting and conserving endangered and migratory bird species, within the European "Natura 2000" network of protected areas.

LABEL: bit
definition: "An information unit which refers to a digit in the binary numeral system, which consists of base 2 digits (ie there are only 2 possible values: 0 or 1)." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: blast furnace gas
definition: Blast furnace gas is manufactured coal based gas produced during the combustion of coke in blast furnaces in the iron and steel industry. It is recovered and used as a fuel partly within the plant and partly in other steel industry processes or in power stations equipped to burn it. The quantity of fuel should be reported on a gross calorific value basis.

LABEL: blended liquid fuel
definition: A blended liquid fuel is a liquid combustion fuel that contains a liquid fossil fuel and a liquid renewable fuel or a liquid biofuel.

LABEL: block size
definition: Block size is the declared net capacity of a power generating unit.

LABEL: BNatSchG
definition: The BNatSchG is a legislation providing the legal framework for nature conservation and landscape management in Germany.

LABEL: boiler
definition: A boiler is a heater that increases the thermal energy of fluids.

LABEL: boolean value
definition: A boolean value is an variable information content entity that can only be true or false.

LABEL: boolean variable
definition: A boolean variable is a variable that represents a boolean value.

LABEL: bottom up
definition: Bottom up is an analytical approach where parts of the system are defined in details. Once these parts are designed and developed, then these parts or components are linked together to prepare a bigger component. This approach is repeated until the complete system is built. A bottom up model is based on a composition approach.

LABEL: Brent crude
definition: Brent crude is a crude oil that is extracted in the North Sea and traded at ICE London.

LABEL: bridge
definition: A bridge is a transport network component that spans a physical obstacle without blocking the way underneath.

LABEL: BSI-KritisV energy sector
definition: The BSI-KritisV energy sector is an energy transformation sector defined by the BSI-KritisV sector division (§ 2 BSI-KritisV).

LABEL: BSI-KritisV sector division
definition: The BSI-KritisV sector division is a sector division by the German regulation BSI-Kritisverordnung (BSI-KritisV) defining eight sectors that contain critical infrastructures.

LABEL: BSI-KritisV transport sector
definition: The BSI-KritisV transport sector is a transport sector defined by the BSI-KritisV sector division (§ 8 BSI-KritisV).

LABEL: building sector
definition: A building sector is a sector that covers buildings.

LABEL: bus
definition: A bus is a motorised road vehicle that is used for passenger transport and has more than eight seats.

LABEL: bus station
definition: A bus station is a transport hub for busses.

LABEL: BWaldG
definition: The BWaldG is a legislation providing the legal framework for the preservation of forests and the promotion of forestry in Germany.

LABEL: byte
definition: "An information unit which is equal to 8 bits." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: C++
definition: C++ is a programming languages designed by Bjarne Stroustrup and standardised by ISO/IEC.

LABEL: calculate economic potential
definition: Calculate economic potential is an action specification that describes the determination of the total economic potential of the available area under a maximum threshold LCOE value.

LABEL: calculate feasible potential
definition: Calculate feasible potential is an action specification that describes the calculation of the feasible wind energy potential, considering both technical and socio-economic constraints.

LABEL: calculate levelised cost of electricity
definition: Calculate levelised cost of electricity is an action specification that describes the computation of the levelised cost of electricity (LCOE) either for individual turbines or for sub-regions within the study area by applying a cost model based on the previously calculated economic parameters and the capacity factors.

LABEL: calculate technical potential
definition: Calculate technical potential is an action specification that describes how the total energy production capability of the available area is determined, factoring in turbine placement, capacity density, and wake losses.

LABEL: canal
definition: A canal is a transport network component that is an artificially created waterway.

LABEL: candela
definition: "A luminous intensity unit which equal to the luminous intensity, in a given direction, of a source that emits monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 x 1012 hertz and that has a radiant intensity in that direction of 1/683 watt per steradian." [BIPM:BIPM, NIST:NIST]

LABEL: capacity premium
definition: A capacity premium is a market premium that guarantees remuneration for reserving capacity of energy transformation units to be available for unexpected events.

LABEL: car
definition: A car is a motorised road vehicle that is used for passenger transport and has a maximum of eight seats.

LABEL: carbon capture
definition: Carbon capture is a process that captures carbon dioxide from a gas.

LABEL: carbon capture and storage
definition: Carbon capture and storage (CCS) is a process that combines carbon capture and carbon sequestration.

LABEL: carbon capture and storage technology
definition: A carbon capture and storage technology is a technology that describes how to combine artificial objects and a carbon capture and storage process in a specific way to permanently store CO2.

LABEL: carbon dioxide
definition: Carbon dioxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula CO2. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and can work as a greenhouse gas.

LABEL: carbon dioxide equivalent quantity value
definition: A carbon dioxide equivalent quantity is a greenhouse gas emission value that quantifies the combined effect of all emitted greenhouse gases by giving an equivalent amount of CO2 which would have the same effect on the climate.

LABEL: carbon monoxide
definition: Carbon monoxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula CO. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant.

LABEL: carbon storage
definition: Carbon storage is a process that stores CO2 in a geological formation.

LABEL: carbon tax
definition: Carbon tax is a tax for emitting CO2 or other greenhouse gases (measured in CO2 equivalent values).

LABEL: carbon tax value
definition: A carbon tax value is a CO2 price that is set by a carbon tax.

LABEL: cargo ship
definition: A cargo ship is a ship that is used for freight transport.

LABEL: cartesian spatial coordinate datum
definition: A cartesian spatial coordinate datum is a representation of a point in a spatial region, in which equal changes in the magnitude of a coordinate value denote length qualities with the same magnitude

LABEL: cement
definition: Cement is a portion of matter that is made from limestone and clay; other elements may be present. It is used as a building material to set as a solid mass or is used as an ingredient in making mortar or concrete. It has a solid normal state of matter. It is the physical output of an industrial process and has a commodity role.

LABEL: centi
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one hundred." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: charcoal
definition: Charcoal is a portion of matter produced from wood via pyrolysis. It has a solid state of matter and can be used as fuel.

LABEL: charging
definition: Charging is an electrical energy transfer where the transferred energy is stored in a battery.

LABEL: checking against empirical data
definition: Checking against empirical data is a validation where something gets checked against empirical data.

LABEL: checking against measurements
definition: Checking against measurements is a validation where something gets checked by using relevant measurements.

LABEL: chemical energy
definition: Chemical energy is energy that is stored in the chemical bonds of a substance, which can be released by a chemical reaction.

LABEL: chemical energy storage function
definition: A chemical energy storage function is an energy storage function with chemical energy as input and output.

LABEL: chemical energy storage object
definition: A chemical energy storage object is an energy storage object that has the function to store chemical energy.

LABEL: chemical energy storage technology
definition: An chemical energy storage technology is an energy storage technology that describes how to combine chemical energy storage objects and chemical energy in charging and decharging processes.

LABEL: chemical energy transfer
definition: Chemical energy transfer is an energy transfer of chemical energy.

LABEL: chemical heat storage object
definition: A chemical heat storage object is a thermo-chemical heat storage object that stores thermal energy by using the chemical binding energy in an endotherm reaction.

LABEL: chemical reaction
definition: A chemical reaction is a transformation that involves the interconversion of chemical species.

LABEL: chemical substance
definition: A chemical substance is a portion of matter of constant composition and that is neither a metal or mineral. It is composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types that is used in or produced by a chemical reaction involving changes to atoms or molecules. It is the physical output of an industrial process and has a commodity role.

LABEL: citation reference
definition: A citation reference is a reference stating where a citation was taken from.

LABEL: client
definition: A client is an agent that receives a product or service.

LABEL: climate neutral process
definition: A climate neutral process is a process that has a process climate neutrality attribute.

LABEL: climate neutrality criterion
definition: A climate neutrality criterion is a plan specification that intends to describe a state in which human activities result in no net effect on the climate system.

LABEL: climate scenario
definition: A climate scenario is a scenario that describes a possible future state of a climate system.

LABEL: climate system
definition: A climate system is a system that has five interacting components: the atmosphere (air), the hydrosphere (water), the cryosphere (ice and permafrost), the lithosphere (earth's upper rocky layer) and the biosphere (living things).

LABEL: closed-loop pumped hydro storage power plant
definition: A closed-loop pumped hydro storage power plant is a pumped hydro storage power plant that has no natural inflows.

LABEL: CO2 emission
definition: A CO2 emission is an emission that releases carbon dioxide.

LABEL: CO2 emission certificate price
definition: A CO2 emission certificate price is an emission price of an CO2 emission certificate that allows the emission of certain CO2 emission value.

LABEL: CO2 emission rate
definition: A CO2 emission rate is a greenhouse gas emission rate that describes the output of a CO2 emission process.

LABEL: CO2 emission scenario
definition: A CO2 emission scenario is an emission scenario that describes a possible CO2 emission trajectory.

LABEL: CO2 emission value
definition: A CO2 emission value is a greenhouse gas emission value that quantifies a CO2 emission rate and has a mass unit.

LABEL: CO2 price
definition: A CO2 price is an emission price of emitting a certain CO2 emission value.

LABEL: coal
definition: Coal is a portion of matter consisting of combustible black or brownish-black sedimentary rock, formed as rock strata called coal seams.

LABEL: coal power plant
definition: A coal power plant is a power plant that has coal power units as parts.

LABEL: coal power technology
definition: A coal power technology is a fuel-powered technology that describes how to combine coal power units and coal in a fuel-powered electricity generation process.

LABEL: coal power unit
definition: A coal power unit is a power generating unit using coal as fuel.

LABEL: code documentation
definition: A code documentation is a documentation explaining and annotating software code.

LABEL: code source
definition: A code source is a data descriptor describing the origin of some code.

LABEL: coefficient of performance value
definition: A coefficient of performance value is a quantity value stating the ratio between the work input and the total output of an energy conversion process.

LABEL: coke oven gas
definition: Coke oven gas is manufactured coal based gas obtained as a by-product of the manufacture of coke oven coke for the production of iron and steel.

LABEL: coking coal
definition: Coking coal is hard coal that is bituminous with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is greater than 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) on an ash-free but moist basis.

LABEL: cold start
definition: A cold start is a process in which an energy transformation unit is started-up after a period of inactivity.

LABEL: colliery gas
definition: Colliery gas is natural gas found in coal mines (British English: colliery). The main component is methane. Synonyms are firedamp, mine gas. It is used as a fossil fuel.

LABEL: combined cycle electricity generation process
definition: A combined cycle electricity generation process is a fuel-powered electricity generation process in which a gas turbine process is followed by an steam-electric process.

LABEL: combined heat and power generating unit
definition: A combined heat and power generating unit is an energy transformation unit that has both the function to produce thermal energy and the function to produce electrical energy.

LABEL: combined heat and power generation process
definition: A combined heat and power generation (CHP) process is an energy transformation that converts energy simultaneously to electrical energy and thermal energy.

LABEL: combined heat and power plant
definition: A combined heat and power plant (CHPP) is an energy transformation unit that consists of combined heat and power generating units, a grid component feeding electric energy into an electricity grid, and a grid component feeding thermal energy into a heating grid.

LABEL: combustible energy carrier disposition
definition: A combustible energy carrier is an energy carrier that releases energy from a material entity in form of heat or work, by chemical reaction with other substances.

LABEL: combustion
definition: Combustion is an exothermic redox reaction between a fuel (the reductant) and an oxidant (usually atmospheric oxygen) which is initiated by a ignition source.

LABEL: combustion
definition: Combustion is an energy transformation in which chemical energy from a fuel is transformed into thermal energy and other kinds of energy, e.g. radiative energy.

LABEL: combustion fuel
definition: A combustion fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by chemical reaction with other substances.

LABEL: combustion fuel transport
definition: Combustion fuel transport is the fuel transport of combustion fuels.

LABEL: combustion thermal energy transformation
definition: A combustion thermal energy transformation is an energy transformation that converts chemical energy of a combustion fuel into thermal energy.

LABEL: combustion-based heater
definition: A combustion-based heater is a heater that increases the thermal energy using combustion.

LABEL: comma separated file format
definition: A comma separated file format is a delimiter separated file format that uses comma (,) as delimiter.

LABEL: commercial sector
definition: A commercial sector is a sector that covers non-industrial commercial activities.

LABEL: commissioning end
definition: A commissioning end is an end time that indicates the beginning of a commissioning time.

LABEL: commissioning start
definition: A commissioning start is a start time that indicates the beginning of a commissioning time.

LABEL: commodity
definition: A commodity is a good that bears the commodity role.

LABEL: commodity role
definition: A commodity role is a good role that inheres in something that is used in commerce and is exchangeable with other commodities of the same type.

LABEL: common reporting format
definition: The common reporting format (CRF) is a sector division used for compiling national inventory reports on greenhouse gas emissions and providing emission relevant data in so called CRF tables.

LABEL: compressed air
definition: Compressed air is air that has been compressed to store energy. To discharge energy, the air is expanded.

LABEL: compressed biomethane
definition: Compressed biomethane is biomethane that has been compressed.

LABEL: compressed gas car
definition: A compressed gas car is a car that uses compressed gas in a gas engine for propulsion and thus is also a compressed gas vehicle.

LABEL: compressed gas engine
definition: A compressed gas engine is a gas engine that uses a compressed gas fuel.

LABEL: compressed gas fuel
definition: A compressed gas fuel is a combustion fuel that has a compressed gas fuel role.

LABEL: compressed gas fuel role
definition: A compressed gas fuel role is a fuel role that expresses that a portion of matter can be used in a compressed gas engine.

LABEL: compressed gas truck
definition: A compressed gas truck is a truck that uses compressed gas in a gas engine for propulsion and thus is also a compressed gas vehicle.

LABEL: compressed gas vehicle
definition: A compressed gas vehicle is a gas vehicle that uses a compressed gas fuel.

LABEL: compressed natural gas
definition: Compressed natural gas (CNG) is natural gas that has been compressed.

LABEL: compressed synthetic methane
definition: Compressed synthetic methane is synthetic methane that has been compressed.

LABEL: compressed-air energy storage unit
definition: A compressed-air energy storage unit is an energy storage unit that uses compressed air.

LABEL: compressor
definition: A compressor is a pump that converts energy into kinetic or potential energy of a gaseous fluid.

LABEL: compressor station
definition: A compressor station is an energy transformation unit that has a compressor to enable gas transport via a gas grid.

LABEL: concentration unit
definition: "A unit which represents a standard measurement of how much of a given substance there is mixed with another substance." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: conceptual model
definition: A conceptual model is an information content entity that specifies variables and relationships within a system boundary.

LABEL: conditionally reserved region
definition: A conditionally reserved region is a region of relevance that has the conditionally reserved region role.

LABEL: conditionally reserved region role
definition: A conditionally reserved region role is a role of a region of interest that is prioritised to be used for wind park projects during the planning process, without excluding incompatible building projects.

LABEL: conduction unit
definition: "A unit which represents a standard measurement of the transmission of an entity through a medium." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: confidence interval
definition: A confidence interval is a data item which defines an range of values in which a measurement or trial falls corresponding to a given probability.

LABEL: considered region
definition: A considered region is a region of relevance that has the considered region role.

LABEL: considered region role
definition: A considered region role is the role of a region of relevance that is used in an analysis.

LABEL: constraint
definition: A constraint is a condition that has to be fulfilled within a calculation.

LABEL: construction time
definition: A construction time is a time span that measures the time that is needed to construct an artificial object.

LABEL: consumer
definition: A consumer is a user of a commercial product or service.

LABEL: consumption
definition: Consumption is the process of using something and thereby reducing its amount.

LABEL: contact person
definition: A contact person is an agent that can be contacted for help or information about a specific service or good.

LABEL: container ship
definition: A container ship is a cargo ship used for the transport of containers.

LABEL: continuant
definition: An entity that exists in full at any time in which it exists at all, persists through time while maintaining its identity and has no temporal parts.

LABEL: continuant fiat boundary
definition: b is a continuant fiat boundary = Def. b is an immaterial entity that is of zero, one or two dimensions and does not include a spatial region as part. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [029-001])

LABEL: contract
definition: A contract is a document that contains an agreement between two or more competent agents to which those agents agree to be legally bound.

LABEL: control area
definition: A control area is a supply grid that is under the responsibility of a transmission system operator and is a part of a supply grid.

LABEL: conventional
definition: Conventional is an origin of energies that don't replenish when transformed / consumed.

LABEL: conventional energy
definition: A conventional energy is an energy that has a conventional origin.

LABEL: conventional energy carrier disposition
definition: A conventional energy carrier disposition is an energy carrier disposition of a material entity that contains non-renewable energy.

LABEL: conventional trader
definition: A trader that trades the power of fossil fuel power plants.

LABEL: cooperative programming
definition: Cooperative programming is the process of two or more people working on program code together at the same time (according to a specified routine).

LABEL: copyright licence
definition: A copyright licence is a licence that states the ownership and contractually sets the rights and obligations to use, copy, and distribute a creative work.

LABEL: cost
definition: Cost is a process attribute that describes the amount of money needed to buy, make, or do a thing.

LABEL: coulomb
definition: "An electrical charge unit which is equal to the amount of charge transferred by a current of 1 ampere in 1 second." [WordNet:WordNet]

LABEL: count unit
definition: "A dimensionless unit which denotes a simple count of things." [MGED:MGED]

LABEL: creative work licence
definition: A creative work licence is a copyright license that determines ownership and permissions for literary work and multimedia work that combines various media types such as text, audio, images, animations, video and interactive content and its collections.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): adipic acid production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'adipic acid production is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Adipic acid is used in the manufacture of a large number of products including synthetic fibres, coatings, plastics, urethane foams, elastomers and synthetic lubricants. The production of Nylon 6.6 accounts for the bulk of adipic acid
use. The main greenhouse gas emitted from adipic acid production is nitrous oxide.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): aerosols
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'aerosols' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Most aerosol packages now contain hydrocarbon (HC) as propellants but, in a small fraction of the total, HFCs and PFCs may be used as propellants or solvents. Emissions from aerosols usually occur shortly after production, on average six months after sale. During the use of aerosols, 100% of the chemical is emitted. The 5 main sources are metered dose inhalers (MDIs), personal care products (e.g. hair care, deodorant, shaving cream), household products (e.g. air-fresheners, oven and fabric cleaners), industrial products (e.g. special cleaning sprays such as those for operating electrical contact, lubricants, pipe-freezers) and other general products (e.g. silly string, tire inflators, claxons), although in some regions the use of such general products is restricted. The HFCs currently used as propellants are HFC 134a, HFC 227ea, and HFC 152a. The substance HFC 43 10mee and a PFC, perfluorohexane, are used as solvents in industrial aerosol products.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): agricultural soils
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'agricultural soils' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): agriculture - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'agriculture - other' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): agriculture, forestry and fishing
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'agriculture, forestry and fishing' is an energy demand sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from fuel combustion in agriculture, forestry, fishing and fishing industries such as fish farms.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): aluminium production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'aluminium production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Aluminium Production covers primary production of aluminium, except the emissions related to the use of fuel. Carbon dioxide emissions result from the electrochemical reduction reaction of alumina with a carbon-based anode.
Tetrafluoromethane (CF4) and hexafluoroethane (C2F6) are also produced intermittently. No greenhouse gases are produced in recycling of aluminium other than from the fuels uses for metal remelting. Sulphur hexafluoride (SF6)
emissions are not associated with primary aluminium production; however, casting of some high magnesium containing alloys does result in SF6 emissions and these emissions are accounted for in Section 2C4, Magnesium
Production.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): ammonia production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'ammonia' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Ammonia (NH3) is a major industrial chemical and the most important nitrogenous material produced. Ammonia gas is used directly as a fertilizer, in heat treating, paper pulping, nitric acid and nitrates manufacture, nitric acid ester and nitro compound manufacture, explosives of various types, and as a refrigerant. Amines, amides, and miscellaneous other organic compounds, such as urea, are made from ammonia. The main greenhouse gas emitted from NH3 production is CO2. CO2 used in the production of urea, a downstream process, should be subtracted from the CO2 generated and accounted for in the AFOLU Sector.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): biological treatment of solid waste
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'biological treatment of solid waste' is a waste and wastewater sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Solid waste composting and other biological treatment. Emissions from biogas facilities (anaerobic digestion) with energy production are reported in the Energy Sector (1A4).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): caprolactam, gloxal and glyoxylic acid production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'caprolactam, glyoxal and glyoxylic acid production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Most of the annual production of caprolactam (NH(CH2)5CO) is consumed as the monomer for nylon-6 fibres and plastics, with a substantial proportion of the fibre used in carpet manufacturing. All commercial processes for the manufacture of caprolactam are based on either toluene or benzene. This subcategory also covers production of glyoxal (ethanedial) and glyoxylic acid production. The main greenhouse gas emitted from this subcategory is nitrous oxide.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): carbide production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'carbide production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
The production of carbide can result in emissions of CO2, CH4, CO and SO2. Silicon carbide is a significant artificial abrasive. It is produced from silica sand or quartz and petroleum coke. Calcium carbide is used in the production of acetylene, in the manufacture of cyanamide (a minor historical use), and as a reductant in electric arc steel furnaces. It is made from calcium carbonate (limestone) and carbon-containing reductant (petroleum coke).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): cement production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'cement production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Process-related emissions from the production of various types of cement (ISIC: D2694).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): chemical industry
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'chemical industry' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Greenhouse gas emissions that result from the production of various inorganic and organic chemicals.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): chemical industry - other
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'chemical industry - other' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
For example, gases with global warming potential listed in IPCC assessment reports that do not fall within any categories above could be reported here, if they are estimated.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): CO2 captured
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006): 'CO2 captured' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories: It encompasses the total amount of CO2 captured for storage.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): CO2 emissions from biomass
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006): 'CO2 emissions from biomass' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories: CO2 emissions from biomass combustion are not included in national totals, but are recorded as an information item for cross-checking purposes as well as avoiding double counting.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): CO2 transport and storage
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'CO2 transport and storage' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Carbon dioxide (CO2) capture and storage (CCS) involves the capture of CO2 from anthropogenic sources, its transport to a storage location and its long-term isolation from the atmosphere. Emissions associated with CO2 transport, injection and storage are covered under category 1C. Emissions (and reductions) associated with CO2 capture should be reported under the IPCC Sector in which capture takes place (e.g. Fuel Combustion or Industrial Activities).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): CO2 transport and storage - other
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'CO2 transport and storage' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Any other emissions from CCS not reported elsewhere.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): commercial and institutional
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'commercial and institutional' is a commercial sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from fuel combustion in commercial and institutional buildings.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): cropland
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'cropland' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions and removals from arable and tillage land, rice fields, and agro-forestry systems where vegetation falls below the thresholds used for the forest land category.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): domestic aviation
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'domestic aviation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from civil domestic passenger and freight traffic that departs and arrives in the same country (commercial, private, agriculture, etc.), including take-offs and landings for these flight stages. Note that this may include journeys of considerable length between two airports in a country (e.g. San Francisco to Honolulu). Exclude military, which should be reported under 1 A 5 b.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): domestic navigation
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'domestic navigation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from fuels used by vessels of all flags that depart and arrive in the same country (exclude fishing, which should be reported under 1 A 4 c iii, and military, which should be reported under 1 A 5 b). Note that this may include journeys of considerable length between two ports in a country (e.g. San Francisco to Honolulu).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): electrical equipment
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'electrical equipment' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Electrical equipment is used in the transmission and distribution of electricity above 1 kV. SF6 is used in gasinsulated switchgear (GIS), gas circuit breakers (GCB), gas-insulated transformers (GIT), gas-insulated lines (GIL), outdoor gas-insulated instrument transformers, reclosers, switches, ring main units and other equipment.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): electronics industry
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'electronics industry' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Several advanced electronics manufacturing processes utilise fluorinated compounds (FCs) for plasma etching intricate patterns, cleaning reactor chambers, and temperature control. The specific electronic industry sectors include semiconductor, thin-film-transistor flat panel display (TFT-FPD), and photovoltaic (PV) manufacturing (collectively termed ‘electronics industry’).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): electronics industry - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'electronics industry - other' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): energy
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) energy is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
All GHG emissions arising from combustion and fugitive releases of fuels. Emissions from the non-energy uses of fuels are generally not included here, but reported under Industrial Processes and Product Use.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): energy industry
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'energy industry' is an energy transformation sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Comprises emissions from fuels combusted by the fuel extraction or energy-producing industries.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): enteric fermentation
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'enteric fermentation' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Methane emissions from herbivores as a by-product of enteric fermentation (a digestive process by which carbohydrates are broken down by micro-organisms into simple molecules for absorption into the bloodstream). Ruminant animals (e.g., cattle, sheep) are major sources with moderate amounts produced from non-ruminant animals (e.g., pigs, horses).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): ferroalloys production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'ferroalloys' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Ferroalloys production covers emissions from primary metallurgical reduction production of the most common ferroalloys, i.e. ferro-silicon, silicon metal, ferro-manganese, silicon manganese, and ferro-chromium, excluding those
emissions relating to fuel use. From the production of these alloys, carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrous oxide (N2O), and methane (CH4) originating from ore- and reductant raw materials, is emitted.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): field burning of agricultural residues
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'field burning of agricultural residues' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
CO2 emissions from urea application

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fire protection
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fire protection' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
There are two general types of fire protection (fire suppression) equipment that use greenhouse gases as partial replacements for halons: portable (streaming) equipment, and fixed (flooding) equipment. The non-ozone depleting, industrial gases HFCs, PFCs and more recently a fluoroketone are mainly used as substitutes for halons, typically halon 1301, in flooding equipment. PFCs played an early role in halon 1301 replacement but current use is limited to replenishment of previously installed systems. HFCs in portable equipment, typically replacing halon 1211, are available but have achieved very limited market acceptance due primarily to their high cost. PFC use in new portable extinguishers is currently limited to a small amount (few percent) in an HCFC blend.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fluorochemical production
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fluorochemical production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): foam blowing agents
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'foam blowing agents' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
HFCs are being used as replacements for CFCs and HCFCs in foams, particularly in closed-cell insulation applications. Compounds that are being used include HFC-245fa, HFC-365mfc, HFC-227ea, HFC-134a, and HFC-152a. The processes and applications for which these various HFCs are being used include insulation boards and panels, pipe sections, sprayed systems and onecomponent gap filling foams. For open-cell foams, such as integral skin products for automotive steering wheels and facias, emissions of HFCs used as blowing agents are likely to occur during the manufacturing process. In closedcell foam, emissions not only occur during the manufacturing phase, but usually extend into the in-use phase and often the majority of emission occurs at the endof-life (de-commissioning losses). Accordingly, emissions can occur over a period of up to 50 years or even longer.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): forest land
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'forest land' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions and removals from lands with woody vegetation consistent with thresholds used to define forest land in the national GHG inventory, sub-divided into managed and unmanaged, and possibly also by climatic region, soil type and vegetation type as appropriate. It also includes systems with vegetation that currently fall below, but are expected to later exceed, the threshold values used by a country to define the forest land category.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fuel combustion
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fuel combustion' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from the intentional oxidation of materials within an apparatus that is designed to raise heat and provide it either as heat or as mechanical work to a process or for use away from the apparatus.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fuel combustion - other
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fuel combustion' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
All remaining emissions from fuel combustion that are not specified elsewhere. Include emissions from fuel delivered to the military in the country and delivered to the military of other countries that are not engaged in multilateral operations.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fuel combustion - other sectors
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fuel combustion - other sectors' is an energy demand sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from combustion activities as described below, including combustion for the generation of electricity and heat for own use in these sectors.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fugitive emissions from fuels
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'fugitive emissions from fuels' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Includes all intentional and unintentional emissions from the extraction, processing, storage and transport of solid fuel to the point of final use.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): glass production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'glass production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Process-related emissions from the production of various types of glass (ISIC: D2610).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): grassland
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'grassland' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions and removals from rangelands and pasture land that is not considered cropland. It also includes systems with woody vegetation that fall below the threshold values used in the forest land category and are not expected to exceed them, without human intervention. The category also includes all grassland from wild lands to recreational areas as well as agricultural and silvi-pastural systems, subdivided into managed and unmanaged, consistent with national definitions.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): harvested wood products
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'harvested wood products' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
CO2 net emissions or removals resulting from Harvest Wood Products.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): heat transfer fluid
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'heat transfer fluid' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Heat transfer fluids, which include several fully fluorinated carbon compounds (either in pure form or in mixtures) with six or more carbon atoms, used and emitted during IC manufacture, testing and assembly. They are used in chillers, temperature shock testers and vapour phase reflow soldering.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): incineration and open burning of waste
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'incineration and open burning of waste' is a waste and wastewater sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Incineration of waste and open burning waste, not including waste-to-energy facilities.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): indirect CO2
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006): 'indirect CO2' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories: It encompasses Methane, carbon monoxide (CO) or NMVOC emissions that will eventually be oxidised to CO2 in the atmosphere.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): industrial processes and product use
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'energy industrial processes and product use' (IPPU) is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
It covers greenhouse gas emissions occurring from industrial processes, from the use of greenhouse gases in products, and from non-energy uses of fossil fuel carbon.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): industrial processes and product use - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'industrial processes and product use - other' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): injection and storage
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'pipelines' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Fugitive emissions from activities and equipment at the injection site and those from the end containment once the CO2 is placed in storage.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): integrated circuit or semiconductor
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'integrated circuit or semiconductor' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions of CF4, C2F6, C3F8, c-C4F8, C4F6, C4F8O, C5F8, CHF3, CH2F2, NF3 and SF6 from uses of these gases in Integrated Circuit (IC) manufacturing in rapidly evolving ways and in varying amounts, which depend on product
(e.g., memory or logic devices) and equipment manufacturer.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international aviation
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'international aviation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories. It encompasses emissions from flights that depart in one country and arrive in a different country.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international bunkers
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'international bunkers' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories. It encompasses international aviation and maritime navigation.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international bunkers and multilateral operations
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) international bunkers is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories. It encompasses international bunkers and multilateral operation.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): iron and steel production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'iron and steel production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Carbon dioxide is the predominant gas emitted from the production of iron and steel. The sources of the carbon dioxide emissions include that from carbon-containing reducing agents such as coke and pulverized coal, and, from minerals such as limestone and dolomite added.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): land use, land-use change and forestry
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'land use, land-use change and forestry' (LULUCF) is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): land use, land-use change and forestry - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'land use, land-use change and forestry - other' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): lead production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'lead production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Lead production covers production by the sintering/smelting process as well as direct smelting. Carbon dioxide emissions result as a product of the use of a variety of carbon-based reducing agents in both production
processes.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): lime production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'lime production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Process-related emissions from the production of various types of lime (ISIC: D2694).

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): liming
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'liming' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
CO2 emissions from the use of lime in agricultural soils, managed forest soils or lakes.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): magnesium production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'magnesium production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Magnesium production covers GHG emissions related to both primary magnesium production as well as oxidation protection of magnesium metal during processing (recycling and casting), excluding those emissions relating to fuel use. In the primary production of magnesium, carbon dioxide (CO2) is emitted during calcination of dolomite and magnesite raw materials. Primary production of magnesium from non-carbonate raw materials does not emit carbon dioxide. In the processing of liquid magnesium, cover gases containing carbon dioxide (CO2), sulphur hexafluoride (SF6), the hydrofluorocarbon HFC 134a or the fluorinated ketone FK 5-1-12 ( C3F7C(O)C2F5) may be used. Partial
thermal decomposition and/or reaction between these compounds and liquid magnesium generates secondary compounds such as perfluorocarbons (PFCs), which are emitted in addition to unreacted cover gas constituents.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): manufacture of solid fuels and other energy industries
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'manufacture of solid fuels and other energy industries' is an energy transformation sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Combustion emissions from fuel use during the manufacture of secondary and tertiary products from solid fuels including production of charcoal.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): manufacturing industries and construction
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'manufacturing industries and construction' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from combustion of fuels in industry. Also includes combustion for the generation of electricity and heat for own use in these industries.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): manure management
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'manure management' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Methane and nitrous oxide emissions from the decomposition of manure under low oxygen or anaerobic conditions.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): maritime navigation
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'maritime navigation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories. Emissions from fuels used by vessels of all flags that are engaged in international water-borne navigation. The international navigation may take place at sea, on inland lakes and waterways and in coastal waters. It includes emissions from journeys that depart in one country and arrive in a different country. It excludes consumption by fishing vessels.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): metal industry
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'metal industry' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Greenhouse gas emissions that result from the production of metals.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): metal industry - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'metal industry - other' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): mineral industry
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'mineral industry' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Process-related carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions resulting from the use of carbonate raw materials in the production and use of a variety of mineral industry products.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): multilateral operations
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'multilateral operation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions from fuels used for aviation and waterborne navigation in multilateral operations pursuant to the Charter of the United Nations.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): N2O from product use
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'N2O from product use' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Evaporative emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O) can arise from various types of product use, including:
- Medical applications (anaesthetic use, analgesic use and veterinary use);
- Use as a propellant in aerosol products, primarily in food industry (pressure-packaged whipped cream, etc);
- Oxidising agent and etchant used in semiconductor manufacturing;
- Oxidising agent used, with acetylene, in atomic absorption spectrometry;
- Production of sodium azide, which is used to inflate airbags;
- Fuel oxidant in auto racing; and
- Oxidising agent in blowtorches used by jewelers and others.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): nitric acid production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'nitric acid production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Nitric acid is used as a raw material mainly in the manufacture of nitrogenous-based fertiliser. Nitric acid may also be used in the production of adipic acid and explosives (e.g., dynamite), for metal etching and in the processing of ferrous metals. The main greenhouse gas emitted from HNO3 production is nitrous oxide

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): non-energy products from fuels and solvent use
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'non-energy products from fuels and solvent use' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
The use of oil products and coal-derived oils primarily intended for purposes other than combustion

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): oil and natural gas
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'oil and natural gas' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Comprises fugitive emissions from all oil and natural gas activities.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other' is a sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other applications
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other applications' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
The properties of ozone depleting substances have made them attractive for a variety of niche applications not covered in other sub-source categories. These include electronics testing, heat transfer, dielectric fluid and medical applications. The properties of HFCs and PFCs are equally attractive in some of these sectors and they have been adopted as substitutes. There are also some historical uses of PFCs, as well as emerging use of HFCs, in these applications. These applications have leakage rates ranging from 100% emissive in year of application to around 1% per annum.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other carbon-containing fertilizers
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other carbon-containing fertilizers' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other land
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other land' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions and removals from bare soil, rock, ice, and all unmanaged land areas that do not fall into any of the other five categories.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other process uses of carbonates
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other process uses of carbonates' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Includes limestone, dolomite and other carbonates etc. Emissions from the use of limestone, dolomite and other carbonates should be included in the industrial source category where they are emitted. Therefore, for example, where a carbonate is used as a flux for iron and steel production, resultant emissions should be reported under 2C1 “Iron and Steel Production” rather than this
subcategory.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other product manufacture and use
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other product manufacture and use' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Emissions of sulphur hexafluoride (SF6) and perfluorocarbons
(PFCs) from the manufacture and use of electrical equipment and a number of other products. It also includes emissions of nitrous oxide (N2O) from several products.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other product manufacture and use - other
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other product manufacture and use - other' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other transportation
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'other transportation' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Combustion emissions from all remaining transport activities including pipeline transportation, ground activities in airports and harbours, and off-road activities not otherwise reported under 1 A 4 c Agriculture or 1 A 2. Manufacturing Industries and Construction. Military transport should be reported under 1 A 5.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): petrochemical and carbon black production
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'petrochemical and carbon black production' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): petroleum refining
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'petroleum refining' is an energy transformation sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
All combustion activities supporting the refining of petroleum products including on-site combustion for the generation of electricity and heat for own use.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): photovoltaics
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'photovoltaics' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Photovoltaic cell manufacture may use and emit CF4 and C2F6 among others.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): pipeline transport
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'pipeline transport' is a transport sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Combustion related emissions from the operation of pump stations and maintenance of pipelines. Transport via pipelines includes transport of gases liquids, slurry and other commodities via pipelines. Distribution of natural or manufactured gas, water or steam from the distributor to final users is excluded and should be reported in 1 A 1 c ii or 1 A 4 a.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): prescribed burning of savannas
definition: The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'prescribed burning of savannas' is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): product uses as substitutes for ozone depleting substances
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'product uses as substitutes for ozone depleting substances' is an industry sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and, to a very limited extent, perfluorocarbons (PFCs), are serving as alternatives to ozone depleting substances (ODS) being phased out under the Montreal Protocol.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): public electricity and heat production
definition:
The CRF sector (IPCC 2006) 'public electricity and heat production' is an energy transformation sector defined by the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories:
Sum of emissions from main activity producers of electricity generation, combined heat and power generation, and heat plants.

LABEL: CRF sector (IPCC 2006): railways
definition:

Emissions from railway transport for both freight and passenger traffic routes.
