LABEL: lignite
definition: Lignite is coal that is non-agglomerating with a gross calorific value less than 17 435 kJ/kg (4 165 kcal/kg) and greater than 31 % volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.

LABEL: lignite power plant
definition: A lignite power plant is a coal power plant that has lignite power units as parts.

LABEL: lignite power technology
definition: A lignite power technology is a coal power technology that describes how to combine hard coal power units and lignite in a fuel-powered electricity generation process.

LABEL: lignite power unit
definition: A lignite power unit is a coal power unit using lignite as fuel.

LABEL: liquefied natural gas
definition: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) is natural gas that has a liquid state of matter.

LABEL: liquefied natural gas truck
definition: A liquefied natural gas truck is a truck that uses liquefied natural gas in a gas engine for propulsion and thus is also a liquefied natural gas vehicle.

LABEL: liquefied natural gas vehicle
definition: A liquefied natural gas vehicle is a gas vehicle that uses liquefied natural gas as fuel.

LABEL: liquefied petroleum gas
definition: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is gas mixture of hydrocarbon gases, mainly propane and butane.

LABEL: liquefied petroleum gas car
definition: A liquefied petroleum gas car is a car that uses liquefied petroleum gas in a gas engine for propulsion and thus is also a liquefied petroleum gas vehicle.

LABEL: liquefied petroleum gas vehicle
definition: A liquefied petroleum gas vehicle is a gas vehicle that uses liquefied petroleum gas as fuel.

LABEL: liquid
definition: The state of being liquid. A portion of matter is liquid has no definite shape but a definite volume (at a given temperature and pressure).

LABEL: liquid air
definition: Liquid air is air that has a liquid state of matter.

LABEL: liquid air production
definition: Liquid air production is a production that produces liquid air by cooling and compressing (gaseous) air.

LABEL: liquid biofuel
definition: A liquid biofuel is a biofuel that has liquid as its normal state of matter.

LABEL: liquid combustion fuel
definition: A liquid combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: liquid fossil fuel
definition: A liquid fossil fuel is a fossil combustion fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: liquid renewable fuel
definition: A liquid renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: liquid synthetic fuel
definition: A liquid synthetic fuel is a synthetic fuel that has a liquid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: liquid water
definition: Liquid water is water that has a liquid state of matter.

LABEL: liquid-metal battery
definition: A liquid-metal battery is a battery that consists of two molten metal alloys separated by an electrolyte. The rechargeable batteries are used for electric vehicles and potentially also for grid energy storage.

LABEL: liter
definition: "A volume unit which is equal to one thousandth of a cubic meter or 10^[-3] m^[3], or to 1 decimeter." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: lithium-ion battery
definition: A lithium-ion battery is a battery that is rechargeable and in which lithium ions move from the negative electrode to the positive electrode during discharge, and back when charging. Li-ion batteries use an intercalated lithium compound as one electrode material.

LABEL: location of model uncertainty role
definition: Location of model uncertainty role is a role of an entity in which a model uncertainty is located in.

LABEL: low electricity grid voltage level
definition: A low voltage level is a voltage level in the german voltage classification system describing an electric potential difference of 400 volts.

LABEL: low rated voltage
definition: A low rated voltage is a rated voltage usually used for the local distribution of electricity. Electricity at this voltage can be converted to a medium rated voltage. The usual producers feeding electricity into the grid at this voltage are smaller wind farms and solar installations. Households are the usual consumers receiving electricity at this voltage.

LABEL: lower confidence limit
definition: lower confidence limit is a data item which is a lowest value bounding a confidence interval

LABEL: lumen
definition: "A luminous flux unit which is equal to the luminous flux emitted into 1 steradian by a point source of 1 candela." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: luminous flux unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the flow of radiant energy." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: luminous intensity unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the wavelength-weighted power emitted by a light source in a particular direction." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: lux
definition: "An illuminance unit which is equal to the illuminance produced by 1 lumen evenly spread over an area 1 m^[2]." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: main activity energy producer
definition: A main activity energy producer is an organisational energy producer whose primary activity is electrical energy and/or heat production.

LABEL: manufactured coal based gas
definition: A manufactured coal based gas is a gas mixture that is manufactured from coal. It is used as fossil fuel.

LABEL: manufactured commodity
definition: A manufactured commodity is a portion of matter that is the physical output of a manufacturing process and that has a commodity role.

LABEL: manufactured material
definition: A manufactured material is a portion of matter that is the physical output of a manufacturing process and that has a good role.

LABEL: manufacturing plant
definition: A manufacturing plant is an artificial object that applies one or more manufacturing processes to produce one more kinds of manufactured materials.

LABEL: manufacturing process
definition: A manufacturing process is a process that produces artificial objects or object aggregates that are economic goods. It involves several subprocesses, which are energy transformations and material transformations amongst others.

LABEL: manufacturing technology
definition: A manufacturing technology is a technology that describes how to combine manufactuing plants and manufacturing processes to produce manufactured materials.

LABEL: marginal cost
definition: Marginal cost is the quantity value that corresponds to the change in the total cost that arises when the quantity produced is incremented by one unit; that is, it is the cost of producing one more unit of a good.

LABEL: marine current energy
definition: Marine current energy is the natural hydro energy of an ocean current.

LABEL: marine current energy converting unit
definition: A marine current energy converting unit is a hydro power unit that uses marine current energy.

LABEL: marine current energy power plant
definition: A marine current energy power plant is a power plant that has marine current energy units as parts.

LABEL: marine current energy technology
definition: A marine current energy technology is a marine hydro power technology that describes how to combine marine current energy converting units in marine current energy transformations.

LABEL: marine current energy transformation
definition: Marine current energy transformation is a hydroelectric energy transformation that converts marine current energy to electrical energy.

LABEL: marine hydro power technology
definition: A marine hydro power technology is a hydro power technology that describes how to combine hydro power units, a hydroelectric energy transformation and oceans.

LABEL: marine thermal energy
definition: Marine thermal energy is a kind of natural ambient thermal energy that is present in marine water bodies.

LABEL: marine thermal energy transfer
definition: Marine thermal energy transfer is a heat transfer from the marine water body to a transportable material entity.

LABEL: marine tidal energy
definition: Marine tidal energy is the natural hydro energy of a tidal flow.

LABEL: marine tidal energy converting unit
definition: A marine tidal energy converting unit is a hydro power unit that uses marine tidal energy.

LABEL: marine tidal energy power plant
definition: A marine tidal energy power plant is a power plant that has marine tidal energy units as parts.

LABEL: marine tidal energy technology
definition: A marine tidal energy technology is a marine hydro power technology that describes how to combine marine tidal energy converting units in marine tidal energy transformations.

LABEL: marine tidal energy transformation
definition: Marine tidal energy transformation is a hydroelectric energy transformation that converts kinetic energy from tidal flow to electrical energy.

LABEL: marine wave energy
definition: Marine wave energy is the natural hydro energy of a wave.

LABEL: marine wave energy power plant
definition: A marine wave energy power plant is a power plant that has marine wave energy units as parts.

LABEL: marine wave energy technology
definition: A marine wave energy technology is a marine hydro power technology that describes how to combine marine wave energy converting units in marine wave energy transformations.

LABEL: marine wave energy transformation
definition: Marine wave energy transformation is a hydroelectric energy transformation that converts marine wave energy to electrical energy.

LABEL: markdown
definition: A markdown is a quantity value that indicates a virtual amount deducted from an assumed or historical price to predict a price in a different context.

LABEL: market exchange
definition: A market exchange is an organisation that has the market exchange role.

LABEL: market exchange role
definition: A role of an organisation, association, or group of persons, whether incorporated or unincorporated, which constitutes, maintains, or provides a facility for bringing together purchasers and sellers of financial instruments, commodities, or other products, services, or goods, and includes the market place and facilities maintained by the exchange

LABEL: market participant
definition: A market participant is an agent who participates in trading in a market exchange.

LABEL: market premium
definition: A market premium is an economic instrument that ensures a guaranteed remuneration, e.g. a fixed feed-in tariff, by paying to the producing agent the difference between a guaranteed return on a good/product and the monetary price for which the good/product is traded on the market.

LABEL: market revenue
definition: Market revenue is a quantity value that represents the income from a trade at a market exchange.

LABEL: market share
definition: A market share is a quality of a market exchange which quantifies the proportion a good to the total amount of goods traded in that market exchange.

LABEL: market share value
definition: A market share value is a fraction value that quantifies a market share.

LABEL: markup
definition: A markup is a quantity value that indicates a virtual amount added to an assumed or historical price to predict a price in a different context.

LABEL: mass density unit
definition: "A density unit which is a standard measure of the mass of a substance in a given volume." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: mass unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the amount of matter/energy of a physical object." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: material climate neutrality
definition: Material climate neutrality is a disposition of a material entity that conforms to some climate neutrality criterion.

LABEL: material entity
definition: An independent continuant that is spatially extended whose identity is independent of that of other entities and can be maintained through time.

LABEL: material sustainability
definition: Material sustainability is a disposition is a material entity that conforms to some sustainability criteria.

LABEL: material transformation
definition: A material transformation is a transformation in which one or more input material entities are, at least partially, physically changed and result in output material entites.

LABEL: mathematical model
definition: A mathematical model is a information content artifact that represents a system and its behaviours mathematically.

LABEL: Matlab software framework
definition: The Matlab software framework is a proprietary software framework developed by MathWorks that uses the Matlab programming language.

LABEL: maximum
definition: maximum value within a set of data values, e.g. in a time step or spatial region

LABEL: maximum value
definition: A maximum value is a quantity value that represents the upper limit of an artificial object or process to contain or transform another entity.

LABEL: measure of dispersion
definition: measure of variation or statistical dispersion is a data item which describes how much a theoritical distribution or dataset is spread.

LABEL: measurement datum
definition: A measurement datum is an information content entity that is a recording of the output of a measurement such as produced by a device.

LABEL: measurement device
definition: A measurement device is an artificial object that is used in some measurement process.

LABEL: medium electricity grid voltage level
definition: A medium voltage level is a voltage level in the german voltage classification system describing an electric potential difference between 10,000 and 30,000 volts.

LABEL: medium rated voltage
definition: A medium rated voltage is a rated voltage usually used for the regional distribution of electricity. Electricity at this voltage can be converted to a high or low rated voltage. The usual producers feeding electricity into the grid at this voltage are wind and solar farms. Industries can be consumers receiving electricity at this voltage.

LABEL: medium uncertainty
definition: Medium uncertainty is a level of model uncertainty at which one can enumerate multiple alternatives and rank them in order of perceived likelihood, without being able to discern how intensely the likelihood varies between two alternatives.

LABEL: mega
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of million." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: megabyte
definition: "An information unit which is equal to 1000 kB." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: megaHertz
definition: "A frequency unit which is equal to one million hertz or 10^[6] V." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: megajoule
definition: An energy unit which is equal to 1,000,000 joules.

LABEL: megavolt
definition: "An electric potential difference unit which is equal to one million volts or 10^[6] V." [UOC:GVG]

LABEL: megawatt
definition: A power unit which is equal to one million watts.

LABEL: megawatt-hour
definition: A megawatt-hour is a watt-hour based unit which is equal to 10^6 watt-hours.

LABEL: melting
definition: Melting is a phase transition from a solid medium to their liquid state.

LABEL: memo item
definition: A memo item is an information content entity about a sector that describes that the sector is excluded from some kind of total and only reported to provide further information (memo).

LABEL: merit order
definition: A merit order is a plan specification that describes the dispatch ranking of power plants (electrical generation) based on ascending order of price.

LABEL: metal
definition: A metal is a portion of matter consisting of an atom of an element that exhibits typical metallic properties, being typically shiny, with high electrical and thermal conductivity.

LABEL: meteorological year
definition: A meteorological year is a time step in which meteorological data was collected and that has a duration of one year.

LABEL: meter
definition: "A length unit which is equal to the length of the path traveled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299 792 458 of a second." [BIPM:BIPM, NIST:NIST]

LABEL: meter per second
definition: "A speed/velocity unit which is equal to the speed of an object traveling 1 meter distance in one second." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: methanation
definition: A methanation is a redox reaction that converts carbon dioxide and hydrogen to synthetic methane and water.

LABEL: methane
definition: Methane is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH4. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and can work as a greenhouse gas. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

LABEL: methanol
definition: Methanol is a hydrocarbon with the chemical formula CH3OH. It has a liquid normal state of matter. As it can be oxidised it can be used as a fuel.

LABEL: methodical focus
definition: A methodical focus is a model descriptor that specifies the primary calculation method used in a model.

LABEL: methodology
definition: A methodology is a plan specification that describes processes that are part of a study.

LABEL: metric ton
definition: Metric ton (t) is a a mass unit which is equal to thousand of a kilogram or 10^3 kg.

LABEL: micro
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of 10 to the power of -6." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: middle alignment
definition: A middle alignment is a time stamp alignment indicating that the time stamp marks the middle of the time step.

LABEL: milli
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one thousand." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: millimeter
definition: "A length unit which is equal to one thousandth of a meter or 10^[-3] m." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: million ton of coal equivalent
definition: A million ton of coal equivalent is an energy unit which is equal to 1,000,000 tons of coal equivalent.

LABEL: million ton of oil equivalent
definition: A million ton of oil equivalent is an energy unit which is equal to 1,000,000 tons of oil equivalent.

LABEL: mineral
definition: A mineral is a portion of matter that is normally crystalline formed.

LABEL: mineral oil
definition: A mineral oil is a fossil combustion fuel that is either crude oil or a mineral oil product.

LABEL: mineral oil product
definition: A mineral oil product is a fossil combustion fuel produced in a mineral oil refining process.

LABEL: mineral oil refinery
definition: A mineral oil refinery is an energy transformation unit that applies a mineral oil refining process.

LABEL: mineral oil refining process
definition: A mineral oil refining process is a secondary energy production that converts crude oil by cracking and distillation into various mineral oil products.

LABEL: mineral oil refining sector
definition: A mineral oil refining sector is an energy transformation sector that covers mineral oil refining.

LABEL: minimum
definition: minimum value within a set of data values, e.g. in a time step or spatial region

LABEL: minute
definition: "A time unit which is equal to 60 seconds." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: missing value reason
definition: A missing value reason is a data item that is used to indicate that data is not available and to provide a specific reason explaining why a meaningful value is not available.

LABEL: MMR sector division
definition: The MMR sector division is an EU emission sector division defined in Annex XII, Table 1 of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 749/2014. It uses CRF sectors (IPCC 2006) and adds further sectors.

LABEL: MMR sector: M.International aviation in the EU ETS
definition: The MMR sector 'M.International aviation in the EU ETS' is a transport sector that encompasses that part of the international aviation that is regulated by the European Union Emissions Trading System.

LABEL: mobility technology
definition: A mobility technology is a technology that describes how vehicles participate in transport

LABEL: model
definition: A model is a continuant to represent a system and its behaviours in a simplified or idealised way.

LABEL: model calculation
definition: A model calculation is a process of solving mathematical equations of a model.

LABEL: model calibration
definition: Model calibration is a process of varying exogenous data, so that the model reproduces the known data (e.g. historical) as far as possible, and thus a part of validation.

LABEL: model component
definition: A model component is a generically dependent continuant that is part of a model.

LABEL: model coupling
definition: Model coupling is a model calculation in which output data from one or more numerical computer models is used as input data for one or more other models.

LABEL: model descriptor
definition: A model descriptor is an information content entity that contains information about some model.

LABEL: model documentation
definition: A model documentation is a model descriptor that contains a detailed description of a model.

LABEL: model factsheet
definition: A model factsheet is a model descriptor that contains a brief description of all relevant model information.

LABEL: model intercomparison study
definition: A model intercomparison study is a scenario study that performs a comparison of several models using a reference scenario.

LABEL: model role
definition: A model role is a a role of a continuant for representing a system and its behaviours in a simplified or idealised way.

LABEL: model system boundary
definition: A model system boundary is a generically dependent continuant that is part of a model and separates aspects of the real world included in the model from those that are not.

LABEL: model uncertainty location
definition: A model uncertainty location is a continuant that has the role to be a location of model uncertainty.

LABEL: modelling software
definition: A modelling software is a software used to create and maintain a (mathematical) model.

LABEL: modus
definition: A modus is an information content entity describing the state of activity something has, e.g. active, inactive or passive.

LABEL: molten-salt battery
definition: A molten-salt battery is a battery that uses molten salts as an electrolyte and offers both a high energy density and a high power density.

LABEL: monetary price
definition: A monetary price is a quality of a product that indicates the value in terms of the amount of money requested, expected, required or given in exchange for something else.

LABEL: monetary value
definition: A monetary value is a quantity value that states the amount of money specified in monetary units.

LABEL: month
definition: "A time unit which is approximately equal to the length of time of one of cycle of the moon's phases which in science is taken to be equal to 30 days." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: monthly
definition: one value per month

LABEL: motion
definition: Motion is an energy transformation where some kind of energy is transformed into kinetic energy, and the bearer of the kinetic energy changes its position or location.

LABEL: motor
definition: A motor is an energy converting component that converts other forms of energy into kinetic energy.

LABEL: motor gasoline
definition:
Motor gasoline is gasoline consisting of a mixture of light hydrocarbons distilling between 35 °C and 215 °C. It is used as a fuel for land based spark ignition engines. Motor gasoline may include additives, oxygenates and octane enhancers, including lead compounds such as TEL and TML.

Includes motor gasoline blending components (excluding additives/oxygenates), e.g. alkylates, isomerate, reformate, cracked gasoline destined for use as finished motor gasoline.

LABEL: motorcycle
definition: A motorcycle is a motorised road vehicle that has two wheels.

LABEL: motorised road vehicle
definition: A motorised road vehicle is a road vehicle that has a traction motor.

LABEL: motorised vehicle
definition: A motorised vehicle is a vehicle that has a traction motor.

LABEL: multi-criteria decision analysis
definition: A multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) is a methodology for decision-making. It is an umbrella term to describe a collection of formal approaches, which seek to take explicit account of multiple criteria, comparing goals and outcomes by assigning weights to various criteria.

LABEL: municipal waste fuel
definition: A municipal waste fuel is waste fuel produced by households or non-industrial commercial activities.

LABEL: nace_ sectors
definition:
The Statistical classification of economic activities in the European Community, abbreviated as NACE, is the classification of economic activities in the European Union (EU); the term NACE is derived from the French Nomenclature statistique des activités économiques dans la Communauté européenne. Various NACE versions have been developed since 1970.

NACE is a four-digit classification providing the framework for collecting and presenting a large range of statistical data according to economic activity in the fields of economic statistics (e.g. production, employment and national accounts) and in other statistical domains developed within the European statistical system (ESS).

LABEL: nameplate capacity
definition: Nameplate capacity is the power capacity stating the maximum power an artificial object, e.g. a power generating unit or a power plant, can generate, and the sum of the power ratings of all energy converting component of that power plant.

LABEL: nano
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of 10 to the power of -9." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: nationally determined contribution
definition: A nationally determined contribution (NDC) is a target description of future greenhouse gas emission reductions prepared, communicated and maintained by a party to the Paris Agreement.

LABEL: natural ambient thermal energy
definition: Natural ambient thermal energy is ambient thermal energy that has a renewable origin.

LABEL: natural gas
definition: Natural gas is a gas mixture occurring in underground deposits, whether liquefied or gaseous, and consisting mainly of methane.

LABEL: natural gas turbine
definition: A natural gas turbine is a gas turbine fueled with natural gas.

LABEL: natural hydro energy
definition: Natural hydro energy is hydro energy collected from the natural water cycle (rainwater, melted snow and ice).

LABEL: nature of model uncertainty
definition: Nature of model uncertainty is a quality of a model that represents the core reason for uncertainty within it.

LABEL: NC/BR sector division
definition:
The NC/BR sector division is a CRF-based sector division defined by the UNFCCC reporting guidelines on national communications for Parties included in Annex I to the Convention.
(https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/resource/cp2019_13a01_adv.pdf, 6/CP.25, VI, Table 2)

LABEL: NC/BR sector: agriculture
definition: The NC/BR sector "agriculture" is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by an NC/BR sector division. It aligns to the CRF sector (IPCC 2006): agriculture.

LABEL: NC/BR sector: energy
definition:
The NC/BR sector "energy" is a sector defined by an NC/BR sector division that includes all energy use that is not related to transport or industry. The sector includes:
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): energy industry
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fuel combustion - other sectors
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fuel combustion - other
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): fugitive emissions from fuels
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): CO2 transport and storage

LABEL: NC/BR sector: forestry/LULUCF
definition: The NC/BR sector "forestry/LULUCF" is an agriculture, forestry and land use sector defined by an NC/BR sector division. It aligns to the CRF sector (IPCC 2006): land use, land-use change and forestry.

LABEL: NC/BR sector: industry/industrial processes and product use
definition:
The NC/BR sector "industry/industrial processes and product use" is an industry sector defined by an NC/BR sector division. The sector includes:
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): manufacture of solid fuels and other energy industries
- CRF sector (IPCC 2006): industrial processes and product use

LABEL: NC/BR sector: other
definition: The NC/BR sector "other" is a sector defined by an NC/BR sector division that includes everything that is not included in the other NC/BR sectors. It aligns to the CRF sector (IPCC 2006): other.

LABEL: NC/BR sector: transport
definition: The NC/BR sector "transport" is a transport sector defined by an NC/BR sector division. It aligns to the CRF sector (IPCC 2006): transport.

LABEL: NC/BR sector: waste management/waste
definition: The NC/BR sector "waste management/waste" is a waste and wastewater sector defined by an NC/BR sector division. It aligns to the CRF sector (IPCC 2006): waste.

LABEL: negative emission
definition: Negative emission is the process of absorbing a substance, usually a pollutant that was emitted before.

LABEL: net capacity factor
definition: A net capacity factor is a utilisation value that is calculated by dividing the net electricity generation over a given time step by the declared net capacity times the length of this time step.

LABEL: net electricity generation
definition: Net electricity generation is a process attribute that equals to gross electricity generation minus the consumption of power stations' auxiliary services.

LABEL: newton
definition: "A force unit which is equal to the force required to cause an acceleration of 1m/s2 of a mass of 1 Kg in the direction of the force." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: nitric oxide
definition: Nitric oxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NO. It is a gas and can act as an air pollutant. Synonyms are nitrogen oxide or nitrogen monoxide.

LABEL: nitrogen dioxide
definition: Nitrogen dioxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NO2. It is a gas and can act as an air pollutant.

LABEL: nitrogen oxides
definition: Nitrogen oxides are a portion of matter consisting of compounds of nitrogen and oxygen. It is a collective term for numerous oxides of nitrogen with a gaseous normal state of matter. They can act as air pollutants.

LABEL: nitrogen trifluoride
definition: Nitrogen trifluoride is a portion of matter with the chemical formula NF3. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It can work as a potent greenhouse gas and has an anthropogenic origin.

LABEL: nitrous oxide
definition: Nitrous oxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula N2O. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It occurs naturally in the atmosphere as a trace gas and it can work as a greenhouse gas.

LABEL: NMC battery
definition: A NMC battery is a lithium-ion battery that is composed of mixed metal oxides of lithium, nickel, manganese and cobalt.

LABEL: non associated gas
definition: Non associated gas is natural gas originating from fields producing hydrocarbons only in gaseous form.

LABEL: non-energy use
definition: Non-energy use is the consumption of an energy carrier without making use the energy it carries.

LABEL: non-energy use technology
definition: A non-energy use technology is a technology that describes among other things how to combine the consumption of energy carriers for non-energy use with other processes and artificial objects or other material entities in a specific way.

LABEL: non-ferrous metal
definition: A non-ferrous metal is a metal that does not contain a significant amount of iron in its chemical composition. It is the physical output of an industrial process and has a commodity role.

LABEL: non-metallic mineral
definition: A non-metallic mineral is a mineral that does not contain any metallic content within themselves. It is the physical output of an industrial process and has a commodity role.

LABEL: non-methane volatile organic compound
definition: A non-methane volatile organic compound (NMVOC) is a volatile organic compound other than methane.

LABEL: non-scattered radiant flux density
definition: A non-scattered radiant flux density is an areal solar power density that measures the direct solar radiation within the extent of the solar disk only (half-angle 0.266 deg).

LABEL: non-sustainable biofuel
definition: A non-sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does not conform to sustainability criteria.

LABEL: notation key
definition: A notation key is a missing value reason defined by the UNFCCC to indicate why data is missing.

LABEL: nuclear
definition: Nuclear is a conventional origin that indicates that the energy comes originally from nuclear binding energy.

LABEL: nuclear binding energy
definition: Nuclear binding energy is the energy that is required to disassemble the nucleus of an atom into its component parts.

LABEL: nuclear electric hydrogen
definition: Nuclear electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with nuclear electrical energy.

LABEL: nuclear electrical energy
definition: Nuclear electrical energy is electrical energy with a nuclear origin.

LABEL: nuclear energy carrier disposition
definition: A nuclear energy carrier is an energy carrier used in nuclear power stations to produce heat for steam turbines. Heat is created when the nuclear fuel undergoes nuclear fission.

LABEL: nuclear energy transformation
definition: Nuclear energy transformation is an energy transformation that converts nuclear binding energy to thermal energy.

LABEL: nuclear fission
definition: Nuclear fission is a process of nuclear reaction or a radioactive decay in which the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller, lighter nuclei.

LABEL: nuclear fuel
definition: A nuclear fuel is a fuel that realises its fuel role in processes that release energy in the form of heat or work by undergoing nuclear fission.

LABEL: nuclear power plant
definition: A nuclear power plant is a power plant that has nuclear power units as parts.

LABEL: nuclear power technology
definition: A nuclear power generation technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine nuclear power units and nuclear fuel in an electricity generation process.

LABEL: nuclear power unit
definition: A nuclear power unit is a power generating unit using nuclear fuel.

LABEL: numerical computer model
definition: A numerical computer model is a mathematical model that is calculated by a computer.

LABEL: objective function
definition: An objective function is an information content entity stating the function that should be maximised or minimised to solve a problem.

LABEL: objective specification
definition: A directive information entity that describes an intended process endpoint. When part of a plan specification the concretization is realized in a planned process in which the bearer tries to effect the world so that the process endpoint is achieved.

LABEL: objective variable
definition: An objective variable is a variable that should be maximised or minimised to solve a problem.

LABEL: obsolete economic value
definition: OBSOLETE: An economic value is a quantity value that is economically relevant.

LABEL: ocean
definition: The ocean is a water body that consists of salt water and is covering approximately 71% of Earth's surface.

LABEL: ocean current
definition: An ocean current is a a water flow within a water body/marine water body/ocean that is mainly horizontally orientated.

LABEL: OEP study factsheet
definition: An OEP study factsheet is an study factsheet hosted on the Open Energy Platform. It is used to access the Open Energy Knowledge Graph (OEKG).

LABEL: OEP user
definition: An OEP user is a user who interacts with the Open Energy Platform.

LABEL: offshore wind farm
definition: An offshore wind farm is a wind farm that is build in a body of water, usually the ocean.

LABEL: offshore wind power technology
definition: An offshore wind power technology is a wind power generation technology that describes how to use wind energy converting units in offshore wind farms.

LABEL: oil power plant
definition: A oil power plant is a power plant that has oil power units as parts.

LABEL: oil power unit
definition: An oil power unit is a power generating unit using oil as fuel.

LABEL: one dimensional cartesian spatial coordinate datum
definition: A cartesion spatial coordinate datum that  uses one value to specify a position along a one dimensional spatial region

LABEL: onshore wind farm
