LABEL: report
definition: A document assembled by an author for the purpose of providing information for the audience. A report is the output of a documenting process and has the objective to be consumed by a specific audience. Topic of the report is on something that has completed. A report is not a single figure. Examples of reports are journal article, patent application, grant progress report, case report (not patient record).

LABEL: request
definition: A request is a process whereby an agent asks another agent for something or to do something.

LABEL: reservoir
definition: A reservoir is an artificial object that stores liquid water and has a dam as part.

LABEL: reservoir hydro storage power plant
definition: A reservoir hydro storage power plant is a hydro storage power plant that has no pump.

LABEL: reservoir hydro storage power technology
definition: A reservoir hydro storage power technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine hydro power units in reservoir hydro storage power plants and a hydroelectric energy transformation.

LABEL: resilience
definition: Resilience is a disposition of a system that represents the capacity of a system to absorb disturbance and reorganize so as to retain essentially the same function, structure, and feedbacks.

LABEL: resolution
definition: Resolution is a quality of a dataset that indicates the level of detail of the data.

LABEL: river
definition: A river is a water body that moves through permanent or seasonal flow process from elevated land towards lower elevations through a definite channel and empties either into a sea, lake, or another river or ends on land as bed seepage and evapotranspiration exceed water supply.

LABEL: road
definition: A road is a transport network component with an artificial surface that allows transport for road vehicles.

LABEL: road network
definition: A road network is a transport network that enables transport on roads.

LABEL: road vehicle
definition: A road vehicle is a vehicle that uses roads.

LABEL: robust system scenario
definition: A robust system scenario is an explorative scenario that describes an energy system that is designed to evolve in a robust way.

LABEL: rock
definition: A rock is a portion of matter that is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter that is part of the earth's crust.

LABEL: ROG
definition: The ROG is a legislation providing the legal framework for spatial planning in Germany.

LABEL: rooftop photovoltaic power plant
definition: A rooftop photovoltaic power plant is a photovoltaic power plant that is installed on top of the roof of a building.

LABEL: rotary heat exchanger
definition: A rotary heat exchanger is a heat exchanger that uses a wheel for a heat transfer process.

LABEL: rotational energy
definition: Rotational energy is the kinetic energy that a material entity possesses due to its rotational motion.

LABEL: rotational frequency unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the number of rotations in a given time." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: rotor diameter
definition: Rotor diameter is a quality of a wind energy converting unit that measures the diameter of the wind rotor.

LABEL: Ruby
definition: Ruby is a programming language designed by Yukihiro Matsumoto.

LABEL: run multi-criteria decision analysis
definition: Run multi-criteria secision analysis is an action specification that describes how a multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) method is applied to areas where exclusions are not absolute (soft exclusion criteria), allowing for weighted decision-making.

LABEL: run of river power plant
definition: A run of river power plant is a hydro power plant that uses the momentarily available hydro energy of a river. It has either no reservoir or just has a small one with a maximum of 24 hours of storage.

LABEL: run of river power technology
definition: A reservoir hydro storage power technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine hydro power units in run of river power plant and a hydroelectric energy transformation.

LABEL: rural population
definition: A rural population is a population living in rural areas, as defined by national statistical offices.

LABEL: scale model
definition: A scale model is model comprising of a spatial pattern of components arranged in such a way for them to represent a system.

LABEL: scenario
definition: A scenario is an information content entity that contains statements about a possible future development based on a coherent and internally consistent set of assumptions and their motivation.

LABEL: scenario bundle
definition: A scenario bundle is an information content entity that connects information about a scenario study and the associated scenario projections on the OEP via the OEKG.

LABEL: scenario factsheet
definition: A scenario factsheet is a factsheet that contains information about a scenario.

LABEL: scenario horizon
definition: A scenario horizon is a time step that is under investigation and consists entirely of one or more scenario years.

LABEL: scenario projection
definition: A scenario projection is an intentional process in which output (endogenous) data of interest are quantified for future points in time using one or more model calculation based on a scenario.

LABEL: scenario projection comparison
definition: A scenario comparison study is a scenario study that performs a scenario projection comparison

LABEL: scenario study
definition: A scenario study is a study that investigates one or more scenarios.

LABEL: scenario time series
definition: A scenario time series is a time series that contains data about a specific scenario year.

LABEL: scenario year
definition: A scenario year is a time step that has a duration of one year and is part of a scenario horizon.

LABEL: SCIG wind energy converting unit
definition: A SCIG wind energy converting unit is a wind energy converting unit that has a squirrel-cage induction generator as part.

LABEL: second
definition: "A time unit which is equal to the duration of 9 192 631 770 periods of the radiation corresponding to the transition between the two hyperfine levels of the ground state of the caesium 133 atom." [BIPM:BIPM, NIST:NIST]

LABEL: secondary control
definition: A secondary control is a frequency control that is centralised and automated. It refers to the control area of one transmission system operator. Secondary control succeeds primary control and operates for several minutes.

LABEL: secondary energy carrier
definition: A secondary energy carrier is an energy carrier that has the secondary energy carrier disposition.

LABEL: secondary energy carrier disposition
definition: Secondary energy carrier disposition is an energy carrier disposition of material entities that are manufactured from primary energy carriers or from a different form of secondary energy carriers.

LABEL: secondary energy production
definition: Secondary energy production is the production of secondary energy carriers.

LABEL: sector
definition: A sector is generically dependent continuant that is a subdivision of a system.

LABEL: sector coupling
definition: Sector coupling is a process of connecting processes from the electricity, heat, mobility or industrial sectors as well as their infrastructures.

LABEL: sector coupling technology
definition: A sector coupling technology is a technology that intends to connect processes from the electricity, heat, mobility or industrial sectors, as well as their infrastructures.

LABEL: sector division
definition: A sector division is a specific way to subdivide a system.

LABEL: sector focused scenario
definition: A sector focused scenario is a scenario that focuses on a specific sector.

LABEL: sectoral emission
definition: A sectoral emission is an emission caused by a certain sector.

LABEL: sectoral energy consumption
definition: A sectoral energy consumption is the energy use of a sector.

LABEL: select appropriate turbine types
definition:
Select appropriate turbine types is an action specification that describes the process of choosing wind turbine models based on site-specific wind characteristics, hub height, and rotor diameter.
Wind characteristics include speed, direction, frequency, turbulence, and seasonal or diurnal patterns.

LABEL: select exclusion criteria
definition: Select exclusion criteria is an action specification that describes the process of defining physical, environmental, and regulatory criteria that exclude areas from wind farm development, along with the application of buffer zones.

LABEL: sender
definition: A sender is an agent who initiates a communication.

LABEL: sensible fluid heat storage object
definition: A sensible fluid heat storage object is a sensible heat storage that uses fluids (like water, oil, …) to store thermal energy.

LABEL: sensible heat storage object
definition: A sensible heat storage object is a thermal energy storage object that stores thermal energy through temperature changes in some medium.

LABEL: sensible solid heat storage object
definition: A sensible solid heat storage object is a sensible heat storage that uses solid materials (like bulk goods, powder, …) to store thermal energy.

LABEL: sensitivity analysis
definition: A sensitivity analysis is the process of comparing different model calculations based on a variation of input parameters (exogenous data items).

LABEL: service
definition: A service is a process that is an intangible activity performed by some agent for the benefit of another agent.

LABEL: service product
definition: A service product is an immaterial entity that has the service product role.

LABEL: service product role
definition: A service product role is the role of an immaterial entity that is the result of a service process, and whose value is determined by the value and the costs of the service.

LABEL: sewage plant
definition: A sewage plant is an artificial object that removes contaminants from wastewater to produce an effluent that is suitable for discharge to the surrounding environment or an intended reuse application.

LABEL: shallow uncertainty
definition: Shallow uncertainty is a level of model uncertainty at which one can enumerate multiple alternatives and provide probabilites(subjective or objective) for them.

LABEL: ship
definition: A ship is a watercraft of significant size that is driving on the water surface.

LABEL: siemens
definition: "An electrical conduction unit which is equal to A/V." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: simulation
definition: A simulation is a model calculation that simulates a process or system behaviour from the real world.

LABEL: simulation configuration
definition: A simulation configuration is a plan specification that describes the technical setup containing simulation components, their connections, and all the exogeneous data necessary to be realised in a simulation process.

LABEL: simulation model
definition: A simulation model is a model that simulates the behaviour of a system without a target function.

LABEL: simulation plan specification
definition: A simulation scenario is a plan specification that references a simulation configuration and contains objective specifications to motivate the planned analysis.

LABEL: single axis tracked receiving surface
definition: A single axis tracked receiving surface is a solar radiation receiving surface that participates in single axis tracking.

LABEL: single axis tracking
definition: Single axis tracking is solar tracking in which a radiation receiving surface is following the path of the sun by roting along a fixed axis. Typical axis orientations are North-South or East-West.

LABEL: single node model
definition: A single node model is a model where a region is represented as a single node.

LABEL: sirup
definition: A sirup is a portion of matter that consists mainly of water and sugar. It has a liquid state of matter.

LABEL: size
definition: Size is a quantity of an entity that quantifies its spatial extend.

LABEL: slope
definition: A slope is a quantity value with a plane angle unit that measures the angle between the plane of a surface and the horizontal plane.

LABEL: social cost of carbon emission
definition: Social cost of carbon emission is the cost the society bears for a greenhouse gas emission value.

LABEL: social cost of emission
definition: Social cost of emission is the cost the society bears for an emission value.

LABEL: sodium-ion battery
definition: A sodium-ion battery is a rechargeable metal-ion battery that uses sodium ions as charge carriers.

LABEL: sodium-sulphur battery
definition: A sodium–sulphur battery is a type of molten-salt battery constructed from liquid sodium (Na) and sulphur (S). This type of battery has a high energy density, high efficiency of charge/discharge and long cycle life, and is fabricated from inexpensive materials. The operating temperatures of 300 to 350 °C and the highly corrosive nature of the sodium polysulphides, primarily make them suitable for stationary energy storage applications. The cell becomes more economical with increasing size.

LABEL: software
definition:
Software is a plan specification composed of a series of instructions that can be
interpreted by or directly executed by a processing unit.

LABEL: software application
definition: A software application is software that can be directly executed by some processing unit.

LABEL: software descriptor
definition: A software descriptor is an information content entity that contains additional information about the software.

LABEL: software developer
definition: A software developer is an agent that creates computer software.

LABEL: software framework
definition: A software framework is a Software that is generic and can be adapted to a specific application.

LABEL: software interface
definition: A software interface is a software that enables an agent to interact with it.

LABEL: software library
definition: A software library is software composed of a collection of software modules and/or software methods in a form that can be statically or dynamically linked to some software application.

LABEL: software licence
definition: A software licence is a copyright licence that determines ownership and permissions for software, code, or models.

LABEL: software method
definition: A software method (also called subroutine, subprogram, procedure, method, function, or routine) is software designed to execute a specific task.

LABEL: software module
definition: A software module is software composed of a collection of software methods.

LABEL: software script
definition: A software script is software whose instructions can be executed using a software interpreter.

LABEL: soil quality role
definition: A soil quality role is a role inherent in a region of relevance reflecting how well a soil, that is part of the bearer, performs the functions of maintaining biodiversity and productivity, partitioning water and solute flow, filtering and buffering, nutrient cycling, and providing support for plants and other structures.

LABEL: solar chemical energy transformation
definition: A solar chemical energy transformation is a solar energy transformation that converts solar energy into chemical energy.

LABEL: solar electrical energy
definition: Solar electrical energy is electrical energy that is energy output of a solar energy transformation.

LABEL: solar electrolytic hydrogen
definition: Solar electrolytic hydrogen is electrolytic hydrogen that is produced with solar electrical energy.

LABEL: solar energy
definition: Solar energy is radiative energy of the sun.

LABEL: solar energy transformation
definition: Solar energy transformation is an energy transformation that converts solar energy.

LABEL: solar heat unit
definition: A solar heat unit is a heat generating unit that has a solar collector.

LABEL: solar power plant
definition: A solar power plant is a power plant that has solar power units as parts.

LABEL: solar power technology
definition: A solar power technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine solar power units in an electricity generation process with solar energy as input.

LABEL: solar power unit
definition: A solar power unit is a power generating unit using solar power.

LABEL: solar radiation
definition: Solar radiation is radiation that is emitted by the sun.

LABEL: solar radiation receiving surface
definition: A solar radiation receiving surface is a surface that is receiving solar energy via solar radiation.

LABEL: solar receiving object
definition: A solar receiving object is an artificial object that has a solar radiation receiving surface as part.

LABEL: solar thermal collector
definition: A solar thermal collector is a heater that converts solar energy to solar thermal energy.

LABEL: solar thermal energy
definition: Solar thermal energy is thermal energy that is the physical output of a solar thermal energy transformation.

LABEL: solar thermal energy transformation
definition: Solar thermal energy transformation is a solar energy transformation that converts solar energy into thermal energy.

LABEL: solar thermal heat technology
definition: A solar thermal heat technology is a heat generation technology that describes how to combine solar heat units, solar thermal energy transformation processes, energy carriers and energy in a specific way.

LABEL: solar thermal power plant
definition: A solar thermal power plant is a solar power plant that has solar thermal power units as parts.

LABEL: solar thermal power technology
definition: A solar thermal power technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine solar thermal power units in an electricity generation process with solar energy as input.

LABEL: solar thermal power unit
definition: A solar thermal power unit is a solar power unit that has solar thermal collectors as parts.

LABEL: solar tracked receiving surface
definition: A solar tracked receiving surface is a solar radiation receiving surface that participates in solar tracking.

LABEL: solar tracking
definition: Solar tracking is a process in which a radiation receiving surface is following the path of the sun on the sky.

LABEL: solar-steam-electric process
definition: A solar-steam-electric process is a solar energy transformation that converts solar energy into electrical energy. It has two partial processes: a solar thermal energy transformation and a steam-electric process.

LABEL: solid
definition: The state of being solid. A portion of matter is in solid state if and only if it has a definite shape and volume (at a given temperature and pressure).

LABEL: solid biofuel
definition: Solid biomass is a portion of matter consisting of organic, non-fossil material of biological origin which may be used as fuel for heat production or electricity generation.

LABEL: solid biomass power plant
definition: A solid biomass power plant is a biofuel power plant that has solid biomass power units as parts.

LABEL: solid biomass power unit
definition: A solid biomass power unit is a biomass power unit using solid biomass as fuel.

LABEL: solid combustion fuel
definition: A solid combustion fuel is a combustion fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: solid fossil fuel
definition: A solid fossil fuel is a fossil fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: solid renewable fuel
definition: A solid renewable fuel is a renewable fuel that has a solid state of matter under normal conditions.

LABEL: solver
definition: A solver is a software that solves a mathematical problem.

LABEL: sorption heat storage object
definition: A sorption heat storage object is a thermo-chemical heat storage object that stores thermal energy by using desorption.

LABEL: source category
definition: A source category is a sector that is defined by a common reporting format.

LABEL: source code file format
definition: A source code file format is a text file format that is source code in a programming language.

LABEL: space requirement
definition: A space requirement is a two-dimensional spatial region that covers the area needed by an object or object aggregate.

LABEL: space requirement for construction
definition: A space requirement for construction is space requirement of an artificial object that covers the area needed in order to construct an artificial object.

LABEL: spatial planning policy
definition: Spatial planning policy is a policy of a German federal state that designates portions of a spatial region to purposes like settlement, infrastructur and sustainability.

LABEL: spatial resolution
definition: Spatial resolution is the resolution of a georeferenced dataset that indicates the geographical level of detail.

LABEL: specific space requirement
definition: A specific space requirement is a quantity value that indicates a certain space requirement per nameplate capacity.

LABEL: specifically dependent continuant
definition: b is a specifically dependent continuant = Def. b is a continuant & there is some independent continuant c which is not a spatial region and which is such that b s-depends_on c at every time t during the course of b’s existence. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [050-003])

LABEL: speed/velocity unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the rate of movement. Speed is measured in the same physical units of measurement as velocity, but does not contain the element of direction that velocity has. Speed is thus the magnitude component of velocity." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: sponsor
definition: A sponsor is an agent that supports a person, organisation, or project by giving money, allowance of kind, services or other help.

LABEL: square kilometer
definition: An area unit which is equal to one million square meters or 10^[6] m^[2].

LABEL: square meter
definition: "An area unit which is equal to an area enclosed by a square with sides each 1 meter long." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: square millimeter
definition: "An area unit which is equal to one millionth of a square meter or 10^[-6] m^[2]." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: squirrel-cage induction generator
definition: A squirrel-cage induction generator is an induction generator whose rotating component is a squirrel-cage rotor.

LABEL: start alignment
definition: A start alignment is a time stamp alignment indicating that the time stamp marks the start of the time step.

LABEL: start time
definition: A start time is a zero-dimensional temporal region that indicates the beginning of a one-dimensional temporal region.

LABEL: start-up speed
definition: Start-up speed is ramping during a cold start.

LABEL: Stasis of Partially Mission Capable Maintenance
state of matter
definition: A state of matter is a quality of a portion of matter that describes the distinct physical form in which the matter exists.

LABEL: statistic
definition: a statistic is a measurement datum to describe a dataset or a variable. It is generated by a calculation on set of observed data.

LABEL: steam
definition: Steam is water that has a gaseous state of matter.

LABEL: steam power unit
definition: A steam power unit is a power generating unit that only has a steam turbine as turbine.

LABEL: steam reformer
definition: A steam reformer is an energy converting component that produces syngas from hydrocarbons such as natural gas.

LABEL: steam reforming
definition: A steam reforming process is a chemical reaction that converts hydrocarbons and steam to syngas. As it converts chemical energy and thermal energy to a different type of chemical energy (and waste heat), it is also an energy transformation process.

LABEL: steam reforming hydrogen
definition: Steam reforming hydrogen is hydrogen that is a physical output of a steam reforming process.

LABEL: steam turbine
definition: A steam turbine is a turbine that converts heat from pressurised steam into rotational energy.

LABEL: steam-electric process
definition: A steam-electric process is an energy transformation that converts thermal energy to electrical energy. A steam turbine and an electro motive generator are participating in a steam-electric process.

LABEL: steel
definition: Steel is a metal that consists mainly of iron and up to 2.14 % of carbon; other elements may be present. It has a solid normal state of matter. It has a solid normal state of matter. It is the physical output of an industrial process and has a commodity role.

LABEL: stock potential
definition: A stock potential is a potential of the stock of a source or sink.

LABEL: study
definition: A study is a project with the goal to methodologically investigate something.

LABEL: study descriptor
definition: A study descriptor is a data descriptor that allows the annotation of study information within a scenario bundle by means of keywords from ontological terminology.

LABEL: study design
definition: A plan specification comprised of protocols (which may specify how and what kinds of data will be gathered) that are executed as part of an investigation and is realized during a study design execution.

LABEL: study factsheet
definition: A study factsheet is a factsheet that contains information about a scenario study.

LABEL: study region
definition: A study region is a region of relevance that has the study region role and consists entirely of one or more subregions.

LABEL: study region role
definition: A study region role is a role of a region of relevance that is under investigation and consists entirely of one or more subregions.

LABEL: study report
definition: A study report is a report that is the output from some study.

LABEL: study report due to legal obligation
definition: A study report due to legal obligation is a study report that is created beacause of a legal obligation.

LABEL: study subregion
definition: A study subregion is a subregion that has the study subregion role.

LABEL: study subregion role
definition: A study subregion role is a study region role that refers to a subregion.

LABEL: sub bituminous coal
definition: Sub bituminous coal is coal that is non-agglomerating with a gross calorific value between 17 435 kJ/kg (4 165 kcal/kg) and 23 865 kJ/kg (5 700 kcal/kg) containing more than 31 % volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.

LABEL: submarine power line
definition: A submarine power line is a power line that is installed below the sea surface.

LABEL: subregion
definition: A subregion is a region of relevance that is in every respect a component of a region of relevance, but never encompasses the entire extent of a region of relevance.

LABEL: subsector
definition: A subsector is a sector that is a part of an other sector.

LABEL: substitution method
definition: A substitution method is a primary energy consumption calculation method that treats renewable energy carriers as if they have similar conversion losses as a specified fossil reference energy carrier.

LABEL: subsurface collector
definition: A subsurface collector is a heat exchanger that transfers ambient thermal energy to a working fluid. It consists of plastic pipes laid horizontally under the ground.

LABEL: sufficiency
definition: Sufficiency is a plan specification for reducing, in absolute terms, the consumption and production of end-use products and services through changes in social practices in order to comply with environmental sustainability while ensuring an adequate social foundation for all people.

LABEL: sufficiency scenario
definition: A sufficiency scenario is a scenario that comprises sufficiency strategies.

LABEL: suitable region
definition: A suitable region is a region of relevance that has the suitable region role.

LABEL: suitable region role
definition: A suitable region role is a role of a region of interest that designates an agreeable location for wind park projects within the planning region while excluding the building of wind park projects in the rest of the planning region.

LABEL: sulphur dioxide
definition: Sulphur dioxide is a portion of matter with the chemical formula SO2. It has a gaseous normal state of matter and can act as an air pollutant.

LABEL: sulphur hexafluoride
definition: Sulphur hexafluoride is a portion of matter with the chemical formula SF6. It has a gaseous normal state of matter. It can work as a potent greenhouse gas and has an anthropogenic origin.

LABEL: superconducting magnetic energy storage
definition: A superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) is an energy storage object that stores electrical energy in the magnetic field of a superconducting magnet.

LABEL: supply grid
definition: A supply grid is a supply system of systematically connected artificial objects that can work as a supply system.

LABEL: supply system
definition: A supply system is a system that connects producers and consumers.

LABEL: surface
definition: A surface is a tangential proper part of an object that extends in two dimensions.

LABEL: surface azimuth angle
definition: A surface azimuth angle is a quantity value with a plane angle unit that measures the deviation of the projection on a horizontal plane of the normal to the plane from the local meridian, with zero due south, east negative, and west positive.

LABEL: sustainability criterion
definition: A sustainability criterion is a plan specification that intends to meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own environmental, economic and social needs.

LABEL: sustainable biofuel
definition: A sustainable biofuel is a biofuel that does conform to sustainability criteria.

LABEL: sustainable flow potential
definition: A sustainable flow potential is a type of flow potential that takes into account all aspects of sustainability, which usually requires careful consideration and evaluation of different ecological and socio-economic aspects. The differentiation of the sustainable potential is blurred, since ecological aspects may already have been considered for the technological or economic potential, depending on the author.

LABEL: sustainable process
definition: A sustainable process is a process that has a process sustainability attribute.

LABEL: sustainable stock potential
definition: A sustainable stock potential is a type of stock potential that takes into account all aspects of sustainability, which usually requires careful consideration and evaluation of different ecological and socio-economic aspects. The differentiation of the sustainable potential is blurred, since ecological aspects may already have been considered for the technological or economic potential, depending on the author.

LABEL: switchyard
definition: A switchyard is an electricity grid component that connects different levels of voltage

LABEL: symbol
definition: An information content entity that is a mark(s) or character(s) used as a conventional representation of another entity.

LABEL: syngas
definition: Syngas is a gas mixture consisting primarily of hydrogen, carbon monoxide, and very often carbon dioxide, that can be used as fuel.

LABEL: synthetic
definition: Synthetic is an anthropogenic origin of portions of matter created artificially by a chemical process.

LABEL: synthetic ammonia
definition: Synthetic ammonia is ammonia that has a synthetic origin.

LABEL: synthetic data set
definition: A synthetic data set is a dataset that is obtained by artificially creating data items. It is constructed to be an estimation of a real-world dataset.

LABEL: synthetic fuel
definition: A synthetic fuel is a fuel produced from one or more portion(s) of matter using electric energy.

LABEL: synthetic hydrogen
definition: Synthetic hydrogen is hydrogen with synthetic origin.

LABEL: synthetic methane
definition: Synthetic methane is methane that has a synthetic origin.

LABEL: system
definition: A material entity consisting of multiple components that are causally integrated.

LABEL: system cost
definition: System cost are total costs of a system.

LABEL: system robustness
definition: System robustness is a disposition of a system that is designed or evolved in such a way as to be resistant to total failure despite partial damage or external changes.

LABEL: tangential proper part
definition: A tangential proper part is a fiat object part of an entity which shares a boundary with that entity.

LABEL: tank
definition: A tank is an artificial object that stores a liquid or gaseous portion of matter.

LABEL: tank ship
definition: A tank ship is a cargo ship used for the transport of liquid goods.

LABEL: target driven scenario
definition: A target driven scenario is a scenario that contains certain target constraints/ statements that in a possible future shall be realized. The path how the targets will be met is not predefined in the scenario.

LABEL: tax
definition: A tax is a levy whose returns are used by the government to finance expenditures for the common welfare.

LABEL: technical model implementation
definition: A technical model implementation is a generically dependent continuant that is part of a model and consists of the hardware and software realization of a (conceptual) model.

LABEL: techno-economic potential determination method
definition: Techno-economic potential determination method is a methodology with the goal of assessing the economic viability of wind energy projects within the available area, based on the technical potential and incorporating cost factors and economic metrics.

LABEL: techno-economic potential determination process
definition: Techno-economic potential determination process is a process that follows a determination methodology for techno-economic potental to gain knowledge of the techno-economic potential of the available region.

LABEL: technological flow potential
definition: A technological flow potential is a type of a flow potential derived from a theoretical flow potential, taking account of the annual efficiency of the respective conversion technology and the additional restrictions regarding the area that is realistically available for energy generation.

LABEL: technological stock potential
definition: A technological stock potential is a type of a stock potential derived from a theoretical stock potential, taking account of the annual efficiency of the respective conversion technology and the additional restrictions regarding the area that is realistically available for energy generation.

LABEL: technology
definition: A technology is a plan specification that describes how to combine artificial objects or other material entities and processes in a specific way.

LABEL: technology scenario
definition: An technology scenario is a scenario that investigates future system states with the focus on a specific technology.

LABEL: temperature
definition: Temperature is a quality representing the driving force for the flow of heat energy and is a measure of the heat content of a material entity.

LABEL: temperature unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a sample of matter." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: temporal resolution
definition: Temporal resolution is the resolution of a time series that indicates time-dependent the level of detail.

LABEL: tera
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of ten to the power of 12." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: terabyte
definition: "An information unit which is equal to 1000 gigabytes." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: terajoule
definition: An energy unit which is equal to 10^12 joules.

LABEL: terawatt-hour
definition: A terawatt-hour is a watt-hour based unit which is equal to 10^12 watt-hours.

LABEL: tertiary control
definition: A tertiary control is a frequency control that is either automated or manual. It takes over from secondary control to equalise electricity supply and demand imbalances that last for more than 15 minutes.

LABEL: test data set
definition: A test data set is a data set used for testing.

LABEL: text file format
definition: A text file format is a file format that is structured as a sequence of lines of electronic text.

LABEL: textual entity
definition: A textual entity is a part of a manifestation (FRBR sense), a generically dependent continuant whose concretizations are patterns of glyphs intended to be interpreted as words, formulas, etc.

LABEL: The Matlab programming language is a programming language developed by MathWorks for use in the Matlab software framework.
theoretical flow potential
definition: A theoretical flow potential is a type of flow potential that identifies the physical upper limit of an input or output of a process in a spatial region of reference per unit time.

LABEL: theoretical stock potential
definition: A theoretical stock potential is a type of stock potential that identifies the physical upper limit of a stock of a source or sink in a spatial region of reference.

LABEL: thermal energy
definition: Thermal energy is the energy that a material entity contains in the undirected motion of its constituent parts (e.g. molecules and atoms).

LABEL: thermal energy storage function
definition: A thermal energy storage function is an energy storage function with thermal energy as input and output.

LABEL: thermal energy storage object
definition: A thermal energy storage object is an energy storage object that has the function to store thermal energy.

LABEL: thermal energy storage technology
definition: An thermal energy storage technology is an energy storage technology that describes how to combine thermal energy storage objects and thermal energy in charging and decharging processes.

LABEL: thermo-chemical heat storage object
definition: A thermo-chemical heat storage object (TCS) is a thermal energy storage object that stores thermal energy through reversible exotherm/endotherm chemical reaction with thermo-chemical materials (TCM).

LABEL: thorium
definition: Thorium is a portion of matter with the chemical formula Th. It has a solid normal state of matter.

LABEL: three dimensional cartesian spatial coordinate datum
definition: A cartesion spatial coordinate datum that  uses three values to specify a position within a three dimensional spatial region

LABEL: tidal flow
definition: Tidal flow is a water flow during which movements of water masses caused by varying gravitational and rotational forces from sun and moon, combined with the rotation of the earth, cause waters to undergo periodic depth oscillations (tides).

LABEL: time series
definition: A time series is a data set that references to a set of time steps or zero-dimensional temporal regions.

LABEL: time span
definition: A time span is a quantity value indicating the duration of a one-dimensional temporal region, measured in a time unit.

LABEL: time stamp
definition: A time stamp is a data descriptor that is used to describe either a temporal region or a data item that is related to a temporal region, e.g. a time stamped measurement datum. If the time stamp refers to a time step/one-dimensional temporal region, the indication of a time stamp alignment is required

LABEL: time stamp alignment
definition: A time stamp alignment is a data descriptor that indicates the position of a time stamp in a time step.

LABEL: time step
definition: A time step is a one-dimensional temporal region that has a start time and an ending time and thus a finite duration.

LABEL: time unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the dimension in which events occur in sequence." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: ton of coal equivalent
definition: A ton of coal equivalent is an energy unit which is equal to the amount of energy released by burning one metric ton of coal with a certain net calorific value. That is defined as 0.7 tons of oil equivalent (toe) and thus equals 29.3076 gigajoules or 8.141 megawatt-hours.

LABEL: ton of oil equivalent
definition: A ton of oil equivalent is an energy unit which is equal to the amount of energy released by burning one metric ton of crude oil with a certain net calorific value. That is defined as 41.868 gigajoules or 11.63 megawatt-hours.

LABEL: ton-kilometre
definition: Ton-kilometre is a transport performance unit for the accumulated transport distance of goods where one ton-kilometre equals the transport distance of 1 km for one ton of goods.

LABEL: top down
definition: Top down is an analytical approach where design starts from the system as a whole. The system is then divided into smaller sub-applications with more details. Each part again goes through the top down approach till the complete system is designed with all minute details. Top down approach is also termed as breaking the bigger problem into smaller problems and solving them individually in a recursive manner. A top down model is based on a decomposition approach.

LABEL: total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international aviation
definition: 'Total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international aviation' is a sector that encompasses 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): total emissions excluding LULUCF' and 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international aviation'.

LABEL: total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international bunkers
definition: 'Total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international aviation' is a sector that encompasses 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): total emissions excluding LULUCF' and 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international bunkers'.

LABEL: total emissions including LULUCF and including international aviation
definition: 'Total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international aviation' is a sector that 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): total emissions including LULUCF' and 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international aviation'.

LABEL: total emissions including LULUCF and including international bunkers
definition: 'Total emissions excluding LULUCF and including international aviation' is a sector that 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): total emissions including LULUCF' and 'CRF sector (IPCC 2006): international bunkers'.

LABEL: traction
definition: Traction is a process of pushing or pulling to drive an object.

LABEL: traction battery
definition: A traction battery is a battery that is used in vehicles for propulsion.

LABEL: traction motor
definition: A traction motor is a motor that is used for propulsion.

LABEL: trade
definition: A trade is a process in which one good or service is exchanged for another good or service or money.

LABEL: trader
definition: A trader is a market participant that engages in the transfer of financial assets in any financial market on behalf of a client or a financial services provider.

LABEL: train
definition: A train is a vehicle that uses railway tracks.

LABEL: train station
definition: A train station is a transport hub for trains.

LABEL: transformation
definition: A transformation is a process that transforms one or more inputs into at least one output.

LABEL: transformative measure
definition: A transformative measure is a process that is an activity that has a direct impact on a specific variable in question.

LABEL: transformer
definition: A transformer is an electricity grid component that passively transfers electrical energy from one electrical circuit to another.

LABEL: translational energy
definition: Translational energy is the kinetic energy that a material entity possesses due to its translational motion.

LABEL: transmission grid
definition: A transmission grid is an electricity grid that is able to transport electrical energy over long distances.

LABEL: transport
definition: Transport is the process of moving people or goods from one place to another.

LABEL: transport hub
definition: A transport hub is a transport network component that allows the exchange of people and/or goods.

LABEL: transport network
definition: A transport network is a supply system of transport network components that enables the transport of people and/or goods.

LABEL: transport network component
definition: A transport network component is an artificial object that is part of a transport network.

LABEL: transport performance unit
definition: A transport performance unit is a unit of measurement for the accumulated transport distance of a number of people and/or amount of goods.

LABEL: transport performance value
definition: A transport performance value is a quantity value that indicates the performance of a transport process in terms of its mileage and amount of transported people and/or goods.

LABEL: transport sector
definition: A transport sector is a sector that covers transport of people and/or goods.

LABEL: truck
definition: A truck is a motorised road vehicle that is used for freight transport.

LABEL: true
definition: True is a boolean value which is intended to represent the truth value true (denoted by 1, by +, the verum ⊤, or wahr (W) in German).

LABEL: tube collector
definition: A tube collector is a solar thermal collector that consists of tubes.

LABEL: tunnel
definition: A tunnel is a transport network component that is built through a certain environment (e.g. a mountain or water) and allows to pass through that environment.

LABEL: turbine
definition: A turbine is an energy converting component that converts energy from a moving fluid flow into rotational energy.

LABEL: turbofan gas turbine
definition: A turbofan gas turbine is a gas turbine that produces jet thrust through its core engine and additional thrust through the connected fan.

LABEL: turbojet gas turbine
definition: A turbojet gas turbine is a gas turbine which produces only jet thrust.

LABEL: turboprop gas turbine
definition: A turboprop gas turbine is a gas turbine that drives an aircraft propeller. It works like a turboshaft turbine but is additionally able to produce jet thrust.

LABEL: turboshaft gas turbine
definition: A turboshaft gas turbine is a type of gas turbine that is optimized to produce shaft power.

LABEL: turns per second
definition: "A rotational frequency unit which is equal to the number complete turn in a period of time that equals to 1 second." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: two axis tracked receiving surface
definition: A two axis tracked receiving surface is a solar radiation receiving surface that participates in two axis tracking.

LABEL: two axis tracking
definition: Two axis tracking is solar tracking in which a radiation receiving surface is following the sun by rotating around two axes. The surface is always oriented normal.

LABEL: two dimensional cartesian spatial coordinate datum
definition: A cartesion spatial coordinate datum that  uses two values to specify a position within a two dimensional spatial region

LABEL: typical day
definition: A typical day is a typical period with the duration of one day.

LABEL: typical period
definition: A typical period is a time series that represents a couple of real time periods that have certain characteristics in common, e.g. seasonal specifications, weekly routines, etc. It doesn't refer to a real date. Typical periods are used to reduce computing time of energy system models.

LABEL: typical year
definition: A typical year is a typical period with the duration of one year.

LABEL: uncertainty approach
definition: An uncertainty approach is a model descriptor that specifies how a model deals with uncertainty.

LABEL: uncertainty of a model
definition: Uncertainty of a model is a qualtity of a model that represents any departure from the unachievable ideal of complete determinism.

LABEL: underground fuel storage object
definition: An underground fuel storage object is an energy storage object that stores chemical energy in form of fuels underground.

LABEL: underground hydrogen storage object
definition: An underground hydrogen storage is an underground fuel storage object that stores hydrogen. Examples are underground caverns, salt domes and depleted oil/gas fields.

LABEL: underground power line
definition: An underground power line is a power line that is installed below the ground surface.

LABEL: unit
definition: A unit of measurement is a generically dependent continuant that represents a standardised quantity value of a quantifiable entity

LABEL: unplanned availability
definition: Unplanned availability is a quality that describes the amount of time a power plant is planned to be operational per year, but is not operation.

LABEL: upper confidence limit
definition: upper confidence limit is a data item which is a largest value bounding a confidence interval

LABEL: uranium
definition: Uranium is a portion of matter that has the atomic number 92. It is a silver-grey metal.

LABEL: urban population
definition: An urban population is a population living in urban areas, as defined by national statistical offices.

LABEL: user
definition: A user is an agent that employs an aid, tool or information system to achieve a goal/benefit.

LABEL: user documentation
definition: A user documentation is a documentation intended to assist users in using the software.

LABEL: utilisation value
definition: A utilisation value is a fraction value that describes the instantaneous share of a maximum value that is utilised.

LABEL: utility pole
definition: A utility pole is a power line support structure used to support one or more overhead power lines, typically constructed from wood, metal, concrete, or composite materials.

LABEL: validation
definition: Validation is the process of checking if something works correctly.

LABEL: variable
definition: A variable is an information content entity that represents a changeable value, vector, matrix or function within a mathematical expression.

LABEL: variable cost
definition: A variable cost is a cost that depends on an amount of goods or services.

LABEL: variable production cost
definition: Variable production costs are costs that depend on the amount of goods or services produced and which are paid by the producer.

LABEL: vehicle
definition: A vehicle is an artificial object that is used for transporting people or goods.

LABEL: vehicle charging station
definition: A vehicle charging station is an electricity grid component that transfers electrical energy into the traction battery of a battery electric vehicle.

LABEL: vehicle operational mode
definition: A vehicle operational mode is a realizable entity that determines how a vehicle is operating.

LABEL: vehicle-kilometre
definition: Vehicle-kilometre is a transport performance unit for the accumulated transport distance of the used vehicles themselves where one vehicle-kilometre equals the transport distance of 1 km for one vehicle.

LABEL: version number
definition: A version number is an information content entity which is a sequence of characters borne by part of each of a class of manufactured products or its packaging and indicates its order within a set of other products having the same name.

LABEL: Visual Basic for Applications
definition: Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) is a programming language based on Visual Basic and developed by Microsoft for use within the Microsoft Office software package.

LABEL: volatile organic compound
definition: A volatile organic compound (VOC) is a portion of matter consisting of organic compounds that is capable of producing photochemical oxidants by reactions with nitrogen oxides in the presence of sunlight. Hence it can act as an air pollutant.

LABEL: volatility
definition: The volatility disposition is the disposition of a portion of matter to sublimate or evaporate from the solid or liquid form and enter the surrounding air.

LABEL: volt
definition: "An electric potential difference unit which is equal to the work per unit charge. One volt is the potential difference required to move one coulomb of charge between two points in a circuit while using one joule of energy." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: voltage classification system
definition: A voltage classification system is an information content entity that categorizes the voltages that components of an electricity grid power system usually operate on, into different levels.

LABEL: volume
definition: A volume is a quantity value indicating the size of a three-dimensional spatial region.

LABEL: volume unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the amount of space occupied by any substance, whether solid, liquid, or gas." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: volumetric flow rate unit
definition: "A unit which is a standard measure of the volume of fluid which passes through a given surface per unit time ." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: volumetric flow rate value
definition: A volumetric flow rate value is a quantity value that has a volumetric flow rate unit as unit.

LABEL: voluntary agreement instrument
definition: A voluntary agreement instrument is a policy instrument that uses voluntary instruments between a government (institution) and one or more private institutions. The agreement's goal is to ensure transformative measures by the participating private institutions.

LABEL: voluntary agreement instrument function
definition: An voluntary agreement instrument function is a function of a policy instrument that promotes, amongst others, voluntary agreement measures.

LABEL: waste and wastewater sector
definition: A waste and wastewater sector is a sector that covers activities related the collection and treatment of waste and wastewater.

LABEL: waste fuel
definition: A waste fuel is a fuel in which the material entity is waste.

LABEL: waste power plant
definition: A waste power plant is a power plant that has waste power units as parts.

LABEL: waste power unit
definition: A waste power unit is a power generating unit using waste as fuel.

LABEL: waste role
definition: A waste role is a role of a material entity that has been discarded after primary use.

LABEL: waste thermal energy
definition: Waste thermal energy is thermal energy that is the physical output of an energy transformation process and that is released into the environment unused.

LABEL: water
definition: Water is a portion of matter with the chemical formula H2O. It has a liquid normal state of matter.

LABEL: water body
definition: A water body is an accumulation of liquid water of varying size on the surface of the Earth.

LABEL: water electrolyser
definition: A water electrolyser is an energy converting component that uses an electric current to decompose water into hydrogen and oxygen gas. Electrical energy is converted into chemical energy (and waste heat).

LABEL: water electrolysis process
definition: A water electrolysis process is an energy transformation that uses an electric current to decompose water into hydrogen and oxygen gas. Electrical energy is converted into chemical energy (and waste heat).

LABEL: water flow
definition: Water flow is a process of liquid water moving.

LABEL: water flow rate
definition: Water flow rate is the process attribute of water flow that quantifies the water volume per time unit.

LABEL: water protection area
definition: A water protection area is a protected area that has the water protection area role, i.e. it is aimed at safeguarding the quality and quantity of water resources, including surface water and groundwater.

LABEL: water protection area role
definition: A water protection area role is a protected area role for areas, aimed at safeguarding the quality and quantity of water resources, including surface water and groundwater.

LABEL: water turbine
definition: A water turbine is a turbine converting potential energy and kinetic energy of water into rotational energy.

LABEL: watercraft
definition: A watercraft is a vehicle that is driving through water.

LABEL: waterway network
definition: A waterway network is a transport network that enables transport on water.

LABEL: watt
definition: "A power unit which is equal to the power used when work is done at the rate of 1 joule per second." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: watt per square meter
definition: "An irradiance unit which is equal to 1 watt of radiant power incident per one square meter surface area." [NIST:NIST]

LABEL: watt per square meter based unit
watt-hour
definition: "An energy unit which is equal to the amount of electrical energy equivalent to a one-watt load drawing power for one hour." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: wave
definition: A wave is a water flow that is at the surface of a water body/marine water body/ocean and that is mainly vertically orientated.

LABEL: weather time series
definition: A weather time series is a time series that contains data about a specific meteorological year.

LABEL: week
definition: "A time unit which is equal to 7 days." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: weekly
definition: one value per week

LABEL: Western Texas Intermediate
definition: Western Texas Intermediate (WTI) is a crude oil that is extracted on US territory and traded at NYMEX New York.

LABEL: WHG
definition: The WHG is a legislation providing the legal framework for water management in Germany.

LABEL: wind
definition: Wind is a process of air naturally moving.

LABEL: wind characteristics determination method
definition:
Wind characteristics determination method is a methodology with the goal to understand the specific wind characteristics of a predefined region, encompassing data acquisition, modelling, and analytical procedures.
Wind characteristics include speed, direction, frequency, turbulence, and seasonal or diurnal patterns.

LABEL: wind characteristics determination process
definition:
Wind characteristics determination process is a process that follows a determination methodology for wind characteristics to gain knowledge of the specific wind characteristics of a predefined region.
Wind characteristics include speed, direction, frequency, turbulence, and seasonal or diurnal patterns.

LABEL: wind energy
definition: Wind energy is the kinetic energy of moving air.

LABEL: wind energy converting unit
definition: A wind energy converting unit is a power generating unit that uses wind energy.

LABEL: wind energy transformation
definition: Wind energy transformation is an energy transformation that converts wind energy to electrical energy.

LABEL: wind farm
definition: A wind farm is a power plant that has wind energy converting units as parts.

LABEL: wind farm area determination method
definition: Wind farm area determination method is a methodology with the goal of identifying and quantifying the area suitable for wind farm development, based on topographical, environmental, and regulatory constraints.

LABEL: wind farm area determination process
definition: Wind farm area determination process is a process that follows a determination methodology for available area to gain knowledge of the available area for wind farm development.

LABEL: wind potential determination method
definition: Wind potential determination method is a methodology with the goal of calculating the technical wind energy potential within the identified suitable area, considering turbine technology, placement, and energy yield factors.

LABEL: wind potential determination process
definition: Wind potential determination processa is a process that follows a determination methodology for wind potential to gain knowledge of the technical wind potential of the available area.

LABEL: wind power density
definition: Wind power density (WPD) is a quantity value of the power wind has in a specific area.

LABEL: wind power density calculation
definition: Wind power density calculation is an action specification that describes how wind power density (WPD) is calculated to estimate the theoretical wind power potential based on wind speed and air density.

LABEL: wind power technology
definition: A wind power technology is a power generation technology that describes how to combine wind energy converting units and a wind energy transformation.

LABEL: wind rotor
definition: A wind rotor (or wind turbine) is a turbine that converts the wind's kinetic energy into rotational energy.

LABEL: wind speed calculation
definition: Wind speed calculation is an action specification that describes how wind speed at the hub height of a wind turbine is inferred from measurements taken at a different height. It is extrapolated vertically to the hub height.

LABEL: wind speed frequency analysis
definition: Wind speed frequency analysis is an action specification that describes the process of calculating the frequency of different wind speed intervals over a set period giving a wind speed frequency distribution.

LABEL: wind variability identification
definition:
Wind variability identification is an action specification that describes the process of identifying variations in wind characteristics across temporal scales.
Wind characteristics include speed, direction, frequency, turbulence, and seasonal or diurnal patterns.

LABEL: with additional measures scenario
definition: A with additional measures scenario (WAM) is a policy scenario that includes policy instruments and transformative measures which have been adopted and implemented to mitigate climate change or meet energy objectives, as well as policy instruments and transformative measures which are planned for that purpose.

LABEL: with existing measures scenario
definition: A with existing measures scenario (WEM) is a policy scenario that includes policy instruments and transformative measures that have been adopted and implemented.

LABEL: without measures scenario
definition: A without measures scenario (WOM) is a policy scenario that excludes all policy instruments and transformative measures which are planned, adopted or implemented.

LABEL: wood
definition: Wood is a biomass from trees. It has a solid state of matter an can be used as fuel.

LABEL: working age population
definition: The working age population is the population of people aged 15 to 65.

LABEL: written name
definition: A textual entity that denotes a particular in reality.

LABEL: year
definition: "A time unit which is equal to 12 months which in science is taken to be equal to 365.25 days." [Wikipedia:Wikipedia]

LABEL: yield profile
definition: A yield profile is a generation time series of a particular renewable power plant.

LABEL: yocto
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of 10 to the power of -24." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: yotta
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of ten to the power of 24." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: zepto
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of 10 to the power of -21." [UO:GVG]

LABEL: zetta
definition: "A prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of ten to the power of 21." [UO:GVG]
